First, the Multi-scale residual gated recurrent unit network (MS-ResGRU-Net) was developed for maize spectral vigor detection, achieving an accuracy of 94.35 %. Second, a two-stage model optimization strategy was employed, transferring deep spectral features from MS-ResGRU-Net to the ensemble learning model, further improving the vigor detection accuracy to 95.48 %. The model facilitated quantitative analysis of vigor-related phenotypic traits and physiological indicator, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.8130 for root length, 0.8057 for root weight, and 0.7876 for physiological indicator between predicted and true values. Furthermore, Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) was utilized to elucidate the relationships among model features, spectral features, and seed vigor traits, providing clearer insights into the model’s decision-making process. This study presents a non-destructive, efficient method for detecting maize seed vigor, offering a novel approach for assessing the vigor of other crop seeds.

title: SmartEars: A practical framework for poultry respiratory monitoring via spectrogram-based audio classification and AI-assisted labeling
abstract: In large-scale poultry farming, respiratory diseases affect the health of chickens, leading to a decline in the quality and yield of both meat and eggs. Effective monitoring of these diseases is crucial to reducing their impact and enhancing the quality and yield. Currently, most monitoring methods still rely on manually monitoring chicken vocalizations, which are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and require specialized personnel, making continuous 24/7 monitoring unfeasible. Existing intelligent methods are often limited to laboratory environments where individual chickens are monitored separately. These approaches fall short of industrial needs, as poultry farms produce complex audio signals including chicken calls, cage noise, human activity, and mechanical systems. In this study, we design a deep learning-based intelligent recognition algorithm capable of accurately distinguishing abnormal chicken vocalizations among complex sound signals. This algorithm was integrated into a distributed health monitoring system - SmartEars, enabling continuous collection of various sound signals and performing real-time recognitions, thereby providing round-the-clock monitoring of the respiratory diseases of chickens in real production environments. We collected 11,686 audio slices from actual farming environments, which were labeled through multiple rounds of data cleaning that combined the objectivity of AI with the expertise of veterinarians, resulting in a high-quality annotated dataset. Additionally, we used Logfbank to capture critical audio features to assist model learning. We also designed five signal-processing-based data augmentations, replacing traditional image augmentation to prevent overfitting and improve model performance. Finally, we compared multiple models on an independent test dataset and selected RegNet as predictor, which achieved the highest accuracy of 96.03%. SmartEars demonstrated its generalization by achieving 80.99% accuracy without fine-tuning and 99.76% with fine-tuning on the public PVSDEDD dataset, surpassing previous state-of-the-art results. We compared the annotation results of SmartEars with 7 professional veterinarians over the same dataset. The results demonstrated that SmartEars with an accuracy of 93% outperformed human veterinary experts with accuracy from 85% to 93%. SmartEars has been deployed in 3 large poultry farms located in Hebei, China, and it has successfully identified a number of outbreaks of chicken diseases, such as a confirmed event around March 19, 2024, March 21, 2024 and September 16, 2024 demonstrating the effectiveness of SmartEars.

title: A lightweight model of dual - backbone real-time detection transformer for pig body temperature detection and its onsite validation
abstract: Pig body temperature is a critical indicator for health assessment of pigs, and can be detected automatically with machine vision-based models, due to their accuracy and effectiveness. However, it is hard to apply them onsite in large-scale pig farms. A primary issue lies in the absence of lightweight feature extraction models that can effectively address the problem of multimodal information fusion. To fill this gap, this study proposes FP-DETR (Frequency Parallel backbone DEtection TRansformer) by integrating parallel backbone and frequency-spatial domain multimodal fusion technology method into the DETR (DEtection TRansformer) object detection model to compress the model structure and enhance the model’s feature extraction capability. The proposed FP-DETR model achieves precision of 98.9% and recall of 96.88% with only 5.9 × 106 parameters and 8.8 h training time. Compared with the YOLOv12 model, FP-DETR improves detection speed by 35 FPS and accuracy by 6.3%. FP-DETR’s temperature extraction achieved performance with R2 of 0.957 and mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.108. In addition, equipment development and model integration have been completed, and an on-site experiment has been conducted, showing that the system is about 42.9% faster than manual. Therefore, the proposed model offers excellent performances of efficiency and accuracy as a promising solution for real-time onsite pig body surface temperature detection.

title: Improved SAC reinforcement learning algorithm: Active control of drive wheel torque to improve energy utilization and reduce power consumption in electric tractors
abstract: Electric tractors are a typical example of intelligent, green, new-energy agricultural power equipment. During field operations, the traction performance is significantly influenced by the interaction between soil, tires, and plowing implements. Addressing the issue of poor control performance in existing non-road vehicle drive torque control algorithms during plowing operations, which results in low overall traction efficiency and high energy consumption, this paper proposes an efficient torque control method for electric tractors based on an improved Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning algorithm. First, an improved SAC reinforcement learning algorithm framework is established, utilizing long short-term memory networks and fully connected neural networks to perform temporal feature extraction and parameterized modeling of the strategy, while integrating traditional control methods to enhance the scope of the reinforcement learning model. Second, a control scheme is proposed, improving the existing prototype control platform, optimizing data transmission. Finally, an electric tractor test platform is established to conduct field trials for validation. The test results show that under the same operational conditions, the proposed control algorithm achieves a traction efficiency improvement of 8.89 % and 16.67 % compared to the SAC and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control algorithms, respectively, while reducing total energy consumption by 5.61 % and 9.73 %, respectively. This validates the effectiveness of the proposed reinforcement learning algorithm and control scheme.

title: CitrusNet: A vision transformer-CNN approach for citrus detection from multi-source imagery with multi-scale feature integration
abstract: Deep learning has become a revolutionary technology in precision agriculture, enabling efficient and accurate analysis for crop monitoring and management. However, variations in scale, resolution, and sensor types across these image sources pose challenges for consistent crop detection. This paper presents CitrusNet, a novel deep learning model that combines the strengths of Vision Transformers (ViT) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to detect citrus fruits in multi-source imagery. In the first stage, we improve the Residual Multi-Layer Perceptron (Res-MLP) based on Swin Transformer, which augmented the model’s perceptual capability across diverse scales through the integration of local and global features. In the second stage, following the application of Swin Transformer, a convolutional neural network is employed to facilitate the extraction of additional feature information from citrus images. In CNN, we propose a plug-and-play adaptive feature fusion module (AFM) that automatically adjusts the weights of different feature channels to enhance the multi-scale feature fusion capability of the model. In the third stage, the model utilizes a decoupled detect head which incorporated Multi-Scale Depthwise Fusion Module (MSDM) to improve the model’s ability to adapt to complex backgrounds and targets at different scales. Using our self-created Citrus Multi-Source Detection Dataset (CMSDD), CitrusNet achieves the experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves precision, recall, F1 score, mAP50 and mAP 50:95 for citrus of 91.20%, 87.16%, 0.891, 94.07% and 84.25%, respectively. It demonstrates that CitrusNet outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and robustness, making it a promising solution for citrus crop monitoring, using UAV, mobile, and AI-synthesized imagery.

title: Multimodal data-driven method for throughput prediction in combine harvesters
abstract: Aiming at the hysteresis problem of traditional contact-type mechanical throughput detection method during combine harvester operation, this study proposes a multimodal data-driven online throughput prediction method. By building a multimodal sensor system that integrates vehicle-mounted cameras, GPS, grain moisture content, and feeding auger power sensors, a throughput prediction framework based on wheat ear biomass characteristics was established: Firstly, the WEC-MVFF wheat ear online counting density map estimation model is designed, and MobileViT is used to build a feature extraction backbone network. The multi-scale fusion module and the centralized conversion module are combined to realize the collaborative extraction of shallow texture features and deep semantic features of dense wheat ears in the field. Secondly, divide the image into regions of interest and establish a throughput prediction model based on multimodal information of wheat ear number (image) − moisture content (sensor) − travel speed. At the same time, a detection model based on feeding auger power is constructed as a comparison benchmark. Field tests show that the WEC-MVFF model maintains an average counting accuracy of more than 90 % under different wheat ear density, travel speed and light intensity conditions. The model’s online counting advantage is verified through ablation study and comparative tests with other counting models. The throughput prediction method achieved an MAE of 0.70 kg/s and 0.77 kg/s in test area 1 and 2 respectively, the first-order difference fluctuation was stable in the range of ±0.50 kg/s, and the prediction frame rate of 10-13fps met the real-time requirements. Compared with the single-modal image prediction method, the accuracy of the multimodal method considering moisture content was improved by 0.80 kg/s and 0.75 kg/s in the two test areas, respectively. Compared with traditional mechanical quantity detection methods, it has higher accuracy and stability while achieving early prediction, providing reliable feedforward information support for the intelligent control of harvesters.

title: RGB-to-synthetic-thermal image translation using generative AI to support crop water stress assessment
abstract: Thermal imaging is becoming a valuable tool for monitoring plant canopy temperature, which can serve as an indicator of crop water stress. However, specialized thermal sensors are often cost-prohibitive. This study explored strategies for supplementing crop water stress monitoring by generating synthetic thermal images from standard Red-Green-Blue (RGB) imagery captured using an unmanned aerial vehicle system (UAVs) equipped with a Zenmuse XT2 sensor and leveraging deep learning models. UAV-based RGB and thermal images were collected from 32 experimental plots of sweet corn and green beans over three growing seasons from 2020 to 2023. Each crop was subjected to one full and three deficit irrigation treatments, replicated four times. A total of 3,400 UAV images were collected over three seasons. Image processing was done in Pix4D software, and orthomosaic RGB and thermal maps were spatially aligned using ground control points (GCPs). The UAV RGB and thermal map data were split into 80 % and 20 % for training and testing, respectively. Two image-to-image translation generative adversarial network (GAN) deep learning models, specifically Pix2PixGAN and CycleGAN, were used to generate synthetic thermal images from RGB inputs. Image quality evaluation metrics, i.e., correlation coefficients (r), mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index (SSIM), were used to evaluate the models’ performance. Crop water stress index (CWSI) values were also computed from measured and generated thermal imageries to assess practical applicability. Generated thermal canopy temperature outputs from the Pix2PixGAN model showed a strong correlation with the measured data using a thermal camera (r >0.95). Moreover, Pix2PixGAN resulted in lower MSE (5.63) and higher PSNR (42.98) than CycleGAN (MSE = 7.09, PSNR = 40.56), whereas CycleGAN had a slightly higher SSIM (0.44) than Pix2PixGAN (0.31). CWSI values derived from the generated thermal images reflected the expected gradients of water stress across irrigation treatments, with the highest CSWI observed from deficit irrigation treatments compared to the full irrigation. These results demonstrate that RGB-to-synthetic-thermal image translation using GAN models could be used to support crop water stress assessment and irrigation scheduling.

title: Estimating soybean yields from high-temporal-resolution multi-source data using deep learning
abstract: Accurate and timely crop yield prediction is crucial for ensuring food security and maintaining stable agricultural markets, yet leveraging high-temporal-resolution, multi-source data for this purpose presents a big challenge in effectively capturing intricate variable interactions across time, especially during periods of extreme weather events. To address this issue, this study introduces an Attention and Graph Isomorphism Network-enhanced Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory network (AGB-LSTM), which is specifically designed for estimating county-level soybean yield in the United States. The proposed model effectively integrated diverse high-temporal-resolution time-series data (5-days), including Near-Infrared Reflectance of Vegetation (NIRv), Solar-Included chlorophyll Fluorescence (SIF), and Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), along with environmental covariates. The AGB-LSTM model achieves an accuracy of R2 = 0.67 and rRMSE = 14.46 %, which outperforms traditional and advanced machine learning methods tested, such as Random Forest (RF) (R2 = 0.52, rRMSE = 17.36 %) and Transformer (R2 = 0.60, rRMSE = 15.80 %). Furthermore, sensitivity analysis revealed the capability of the model for accurate and stable yield prediction 1 to 2 months before harvest. Notably, utilizing data with finer temporal resolution (5-day and monthly composite data) continuously improves performance. Specifically, the model performance is R2 = 0.67 and rRMSE = 14.46 % for the 5-day data, and R2 = 0.55 and rRMSE = 16.81 % for the 30-day data. We also highlight the robustness of the model under extreme climate events, maintaining strong performance with R2 = 0.50 and rRMSE = 21.32 %. Finally, the validation against USDA reported yields for major North American soybean regions in 2023 show that AGB-LSTM well captures the spatial patterns of soybean yield. These findings underscore the AGB-LSTM model as a promising and effective method for yield estimation, showcasing large potential for global crop yield forecasting.

title: SIFNet: A spectrum-image fusion neural network in hyperspectral imaging for intelligent quality assessment of crude tea to ensure tea product availability
abstract: Accurately assessing the quality of crude tea (primary processed tea) is critical for ensuring the standardization and consistent supply of tea products. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) has emerged as a powerful data-driven technology that utilizes molecular fingerprint spectra and spatial image information for rapid quality assessment of crude tea. However, spectral overlap and image similarity between different grades hinder the performance of traditional classification methods. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel spectrum-image fusion neural network (SIFNet) that tackles spectral dependency and subtle inter-grade differences in image features. SIFNet consists of a spectral feature extraction branch and an image feature extraction branch. The spectral feature extraction combines one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory networks (Bi-LSTM) to capture spectral dependencies. While the image feature extraction branch employs two-dimensional CNN (2D-CNN) and fuzzy operation modules to capture both precise and fuzzy image features. Finally, cross-modal features are fused using fully connected layers to improve classification performance. Five-fold cross-validation on the crude Wuyi rock tea hyperspectral image dataset demonstrated that SIFNet achieved an accuracy of 96.75 ± 2.27%, outperforming other state-of-the-art machine learning and deep learning algorithms. This study proposed a data-driven approach for intelligent quality assessment of crude tea, providing robust technical support for enhancing the sustainable supply capacity of the tea industry.

title: Mechanism-guided deep learning for pest classification in tomato leaves
abstract: Tomato, a vital global crop, faces severe annual yield losses of 20–40% due to the pest stress, while conventional identification methods often fail to detect early infections before visible symptoms emerge. To overcome the limited sensitivity and generalizability of image-based approaches, this article proposed a tomato pest stress classification method based on a mechanism-guided hybrid network (MGHN) to provide the theoretical foundation for real-time early-warning systems. We first extracted three mechanism-driven features including transient change rates, pulse amplitude/frequency and baseline offset from the dynamics of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA). These features were then fused with a 1D-CNN to classify the three pest types including piercing-sucking, chewing and crawling-feeding pests. Results show that our proposed MGHN method achieves 94.8% average accuracy on 135 independent test samples, with significantly optimized recognition for piercing-sucking pests (95.56% F1), chewing pests (94.50% F1), and crawling-feeding pests (94.37% F1). Comparative analysis against traditional 1D-CNN and a mechanism-only model demonstrates that MGHN outperformed 1D-CNN (91.1%) and the mechanism-only model (89.6%) by 3.7% and 5.2%, respectively. This research can establish a theoretical foundation for real-time early pest stress warning systems of crops using wearable sensors.

title: Noise-enhanced conditional diffusion model for crop disease image generation and augmentation
abstract: In agriculture, crop diseases have always been the core research direction. To address the lack of crop disease images, similar disease images between classes, and different disease images within classes, this paper proposes a noise-enhanced conditional diffusion model (NECD) for crop disease image generation and augmentation. First, a prior condition feature extraction module is proposed on the basis of the diffusion model. Prior information of crop diseases is formed by constructing an image–text transformation mechanism, enhancing the diversity of generated conditions. Then, with the obtained prior information of crop diseases taken as the conditional text, a dual-condition noise-enhanced method (DCNE) is proposed to enhance the restoration effect of image details in the reverse diffusion process. Finally, a memory enhancement module based on self-attention is proposed for the long sequence generation performance of the model to optimize the long-term information lost in the diffusion process of DCNE. Experiments demonstrate that NECD can achieve a CLIP score of 0.3014 and 0.2969 and an FID of 22.68 and 22.94 on the PlantVillage and AI Challenger datasets, respectively, which proves its effectiveness.

title: Frequency-aware deep learning for diarrheal feces and floor fouling monitoring in pig pens
abstract: Floor fouling monitoring in pig facilities is essential for early disease detection and environmental hygiene management, as diarrheal feces indicates digestive disorders while manure accumulation directly impacts animal health and welfare. Current manual inspection methods are labor-intensive and subjective, while existing computer vision approaches suffer from unstable color features under varying lighting conditions and misclassification of background textures as fouling patterns. To address these challenges, we propose FreCANet, a frequency-aware deep learning framework that achieves multi-level fouling classification through hierarchical visual interference suppression. The method integrates three key innovations: Mask R-CNN preprocessing that eliminates pig body occlusion (improving detection recall by up to 17.21%), Frequency Dynamic Convolution that separates manure contamination features from environmental noise across different frequency bands, and Efficient Channel Attention embedded within residual connections for selective feature enhancement. Using a comprehensive dataset of 25,228 images covering seven fouling categories across the complete growth cycle, FreCANet achieved 88.31% accuracy and 0.8679 F1-Score, outperforming ResNet-152 by 2.44% and 2.93% respectively. Diarrheal feces detection reached 95.9% precision on slatted floors and 89.3% recall on solid floors, enabling reliable early warning for digestive health issues. The four-level manure contamination classification achieved 77.2–87.4% precision across fouling gradients from clean to severely soiled conditions. These results demonstrate FreCANet’s effectiveness in transforming subjective manual inspection into quantitative pen hygiene assessment for precision livestock farming applications.

title: Generative AI-enhanced multi-domain acoustic fusion for real-time recovery monitoring in smart aquaculture transportation
abstract: Transportation-induced mortality from crowding, hypoxia, and handling stress costs aquaculture billions annually. Although anesthetic protocols mitigate these stressors, the anesthetic recovery phase remains critical for timely interventions. Invasive bioimpedance sensors introduce infection risks, computer vision fails in turbid water. Acoustic techniques demonstrate advantages yet face inadequate feature representation and severe dataset scarcity. To address these interdependent challenges confronting acoustic monitoring, this work presents a novel framework combining generative artificial intelligence (GAI) synthesis with multi-domain fusion for recovery stage discrimination. Specifically, Domain-Specific Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DS-DDPM), synthesize biologically-authentic features across Zero-Crossing Rate (ZCR), Gammatone, Phase, and Wavelet domains, addressing data scarcity while preserving physiological validity. Subsequently, an adaptive progressive fusion strategy organizes features into periodicity and intensity groups, integrating complementary respiratory patterns through attention mechanisms. The lightweight MambaVision-MDF (Multi-Domain Fusion) architecture then processes the augmented fused features through dual-path temporal-spectral scanning mechanism for discrimination. Experimental validation on bighead carp demonstrates that adaptive progressive fusion and DS-DDPM augmentation improve classification accuracy by 2.1 and 3.5 percentage points over direct four-domain combination and baseline training respectively. This advancement achieves 96.8% accuracy with only 5.83 M parameters for edge deployment, facilitating temporal-state dual-driven strategies for smart aquaculture transportation management. Meanwhile, it establishes a replicable paradigm for GAI applications addressing insufficient representation and data constraints in agricultural monitoring.

title: Detection of Potato Virus Y in plant foliage using convolutional neural network classifiers and hyperspectral imagery
abstract: Solanum tuberosum (potato) is one of the most important global food crops relative to economic opportunities and food security. Potato Virus Y (Potyviridae, PVY), a detrimental plant pathogen propagated by insect vectors, negatively affects tuber yield and quality. This has forced industry stakeholders to adopt many different types of mitigation strategies including pesticide applications, manual field scouting, and potato seed certification programs. Despite these efforts, PVY continues to disrupt industry production regions resulting in significant economic losses due to the lack of robust diagnostic tools. Machine learning algorithms trained on remotely sensed spectral features show promise as a diagnostic tool for many plant diseases including PVY. This study proposes a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture to detect potato plant canopy regions of plants infected with PVY based on unmanned aerial system (UAS) hyperspectral pixel features comprised of bands matching the center wavelengths of nine spectral channels captured by the European Space Agency’s Sentinel 2 multispectral instrument. Accuracy and F1 metrics of 0.815 and 0.766 respectively were achieved on test data collected over multiple growing seasons and locations. Additionally, efforts were made to identify optimal combinations of spectral bands that are most beneficial for the CNN classifier by evaluating every possible combination of the nine spectral wavelengths in groups ranging from 3 to 9 channels. Results show that hyperspectral channels centered on 783 nm, 739 nm, and 560 nm are the most important features for the CNN architecture. Additionally, six hyperspectral features consisting of the three previously mentioned along with 665 nm, 704 nm, and 864 nm yielded the best results of all possible combinations achieving accuracy and F1 Score metrics of 0.833 and 0.791 respectively.

title: Non-destructive monitoring method for protected-lettuce yield using deep learning
abstract: Accurate acquisition of phenotypic characteristics in protected crops is a crucial prerequisite for intelligent control and digital breeding in greenhouses. To accurately assess the phenotypic traits of protected lettuce, a specialized in situ phenotypic detection method has been developed. The Multimodal Features and Attention Mechanism for Phenotype Detection Model (MFAMNet) was developed for protected lettuce, employing a segmented multi-source image dataset for synchronous regression testing. The results revealed that the predicted values generated by MFAMNet exhibited a strong correlation with the measured values, achieving coefficients of determination of 0.96, 0.92, 0.95, 0.94, and 0.95 for plant height, crown width, leaf area, fresh weight, and dry weight, respectively. Ablation tests demonstrated that the deep learning detection framework based on multi-modal feature fusion significantly outperformed single-feature detection models, highlighting the advantages of integrating diverse data modalities. In addition, the multi-modal feature attention mechanism (MMF) facilitates both inter-modality and intra-modality interactions by capturing the global correlations between modalities and employing dynamic sparse spatial attention. The effectiveness of MMF has been validated through comparative experiments, demonstrating its suitability for the phenotypic detection of artificially cultivated lettuce. In summary, the method proposed in this study facilitates real-time monitoring of facility crops, enabling precise control of environmental parameters in protected agriculture and optimizing resource allocation. This approach contributes to the development of a comprehensive intelligent agriculture system and establishes a foundation for unmanned farms.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for unmanned farming dynamic multi-task allocation problem
abstract: Efficient and scalable multi-task allocation presents a fundamental challenge in multi-machine cooperative operation for unmanned farming. Conventional approaches often assume static attributes and fixed-scale instances, thereby facing significant challenges in adapting to the dynamic characteristics of agricultural production processes. To address the dynamic multi-task allocation problem with time windows (DMAPTW), we propose a novel RL framework that automatically learns high-quality scheduling policies. A scale-agnostic representation mechanism is designed to accurately reflect the current system status, ensuring that the derived policy network is scale-agnostic. To enhance adaptability across diverse production environments, a combination method integrating problem-specific dispatching rules is implemented. Concurrently, a dense reward mechanism is proposed to directly associate the optimization objective. Numerical experiments conducted on a comprehensive set of synthetic instances demonstrate that the proposed algorithm exhibits robust flexibility in handling varying production configurations. Furthermore, comparative analyses reveal that this algorithm consistently outperforms meta-heuristic baselines by 28%–40%, indicating superior computational efficiency and robustness.

title: A hierarchical foundation model framework for generalizable agricultural and crop parcel delineation
abstract: Precise, multi-scale mapping of agricultural landscapes—ranging from management-oriented Agricultural Parcels (APs) to fine-grained Crop Parcels (CPs)—is critical for land administration and precision agriculture. However, automated delineation remains challenging due to the accuracy limitations and poor generalizability of existing methods. While the Segment Anything Model (SAM) offers powerful zero-shot segmentation capabilities, its direct application is hindered by a lack of semantic awareness, a domain gap with RS imagery, and the prohibitive costs of full fine-tuning. To address these limitations, this study introduces PT-PEFT SAM, a novel framework that efficiently adapts SAM for agricultural mapping. A sequential “guide-then-specialize” adaptation strategy is employed, utilizing Prefix-Tuning (PT) to align SAM’s representations with the remote sensing domain, followed by a proposed Orthogonalized Multi-Low-Rank Adaptation (Ortho-Multi-LoRA) to inject task-specific semantics efficiently. The framework is further augmented by a learnable spectral adaptation module for multi-band compatibility and a domain-invariant feature learning module to enhance intrinsic generalization. Furthermore, a hierarchical architecture is introduced: the fine-tuned model performs semantic AP delineation, while a fully automated pipeline leveraging the pre-trained SAM 2 is deployed for intra-parcel CP segmentation, exploiting its superior zero-shot capabilities. Evaluations across European and Chinese datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy (Boundary F1 > 0.92 for APs; Geometric Error [GTC] < 0.065 for CPs) and exceptional transfer learning performance. This research establishes a principled, scalable paradigm for adapting foundation models to specialized geospatial tasks, enabling the rapid and accurate generation of critical agricultural data.

title: Collaborative control mechanism based on reinforcement learning and game theory: Effectively improving the operational quality of electric tractor ploughing units
abstract: Smart agriculture demands higher precision and intelligence in agricultural machinery operations. In traditional control theory, this relies on complex, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamics modelling. Reinforcement learning and game theory can be employed to eliminate the need to develop complex dynamics control models. In this paper, static cooperative game theory is used to analyze the synergistic interactions between the hitch and drive subsystems under the integrated control objectives. A ploughing unit drive system efficiency model and an operating speed model are established to calculate the Shapley values for each subsystem. A reward allocation strategy for the hitch-and-drive systems is proposed, and an electric tractor agent collaborative control method is constructed based on the improved soft actor–critic (SAC) algorithm. Field tests on real vehicles demonstrate that the reinforcement learning control method outperforms traditional force–position integrated control. The reinforcement learning control method increases the operating speed and the ploughing depth tracking accuracy by 28.57% and 13.44%, respectively. This method also increases operational speed and ploughing depth stability by 55% and 20%, respectively, and increases the average drive motor efficiency by 2.88%. Reinforcement learning theory is used to address the collaborative control problem of electric tractors, providing an effective method to increase both operational efficiency and adaptability to changing work conditions.

title: Bridging laboratory and field hyperspectral analysis for early detection of potato late blight using Machine learning
abstract: The potato is a vital crop to the economy and agricultural sector. However, it is susceptible to diseases such as late blight. This disease causes enormous economic losses every year, largely due to the difficulty of controlling it in the field, as innovative technology and solutions are limited. Novel techniques, such as hyperspectral analysis and machine learning models, have demonstrated enormous potential in proposing reliable and non-invasive solutions to address this issue. Therefore, this study aimed to detect late blight foliar symptoms in Diacol Capiro potatoes early by integrating these two technologies. Additionally, given that most hyperspectral studies are currently conducted under laboratory conditions, this work addressed the fusion of laboratory and field work to demonstrate the feasibility of using both approaches for a single purpose: to propose novel tools that support the control and detection of late blight in potatoes. As a result, an early detection model for late blight in field-grown potatoes was achieved with an overall accuracy of over 93%, demonstrating the enormous potential of spectral technology and machine learning models to characterise invisible symptoms of a disease that continues to cause so much damage to the potato sector.

title: Deep learning-powered diagnosis of greenhouse tomato growth using time-series RGB images
abstract: Accurate and real-time diagnosis of nitrogen (N) status is critical for precision management in greenhouse tomato production. In this study, a robust and generalizable critical nitrogen concentration (Nc) dilution curve (Nc = 3.19 × AGB−0.20) was first established using a Bayesian approach based on above-ground biomass (AGB) across diverse genotype × environment × nitrogen management scenarios. The unified Nc curve reduced parameter uncertainty and enabled consistent estimation of the nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) across fruit types and growing seasons. Building on this physiological foundation, this study further developed a physiologically informed multimodal deep learning framework by integrating time-series RGB imagery, SPAD measurements, air temperature, and phenological stage information. Built on a CNN-Transformer architecture, the framework incorporates i) temporal modality alignment to synchronize heterogeneous data streams, ii) growth-stage-aware weighting to emphasize phenologically relevant inputs, and iii) semantic feature enhancement to better link visual information with crop physiological status. On an independent test dataset, the proposed model achieved an R2 of 0.89 with an RMSE of 0.043, outperforming a single-frame CNN baseline (R2 = 0.78, RMSE = 0.072). Modality contribution analysis indicated that RGB imagery, temperature, and SPAD measurements accounted for approximately 52.3%, 29.6%, and 18.1% of model performance, respectively, consistent with SHAP-based importance rankings. Temporal importance analysis further revealed dominant contributions of RGB features during early to mid-growth stages (t2 ∼ t4), with increased relevance of temperature and SPAD at later phenological stages (t7 ∼ t8). These results demonstrate the potential of physiology-informed deep learning for interpretable, stage-sensitive nitrogen monitoring in controlled-environment agriculture.

title: Physics-guided spatiotemporal graph transformer for explainable detection and risk forecasting of mold and condensation in grain storage
abstract: Accurate identification and early warning of mold and condensation risks in grain storage are essential for ensuring grain security. However, existing approaches often fail to adequately capture spatiotemporal dependencies, integrate multimodal information, deliver forward-looking warnings, or offer sufficient interpretability. To address these challenges, a physics-guided spatiotemporal graph Transformer is proposed for abnormal condition detection and risk forecasting, thereby supporting the transition of grain storage monitoring from passive surveillance to proactive and trustworthy risk management. The framework is built on a Graph Convolutional Network-Temporal Fusion Transformer (GCN-TFT) backbone, where graph convolutions explicitly encode spatial dependencies within the grain bulk temperature field, while a TFT integrates multi-source heterogeneous inputs. Mechanistic features encoding temporal continuity, spatial continuity, seasonal periodicity, and dew-point criteria are incorporated to enable joint modeling of physical constraints and data-driven representations. On this basis, a forecast-aware attention (FAA) risk head is introduced, which uses the current spatiotemporal representation as a query and performs cross-attention with future meteorological forecasts, thereby conditioning interval-wise risk estimates on potential future warm and humid conditions. A training strategy combining self-supervised spatiotemporal pretraining with fine-tuning on a limited set of labeled samples is employed to mitigate the impact of label scarcity for abnormal modalities and class imbalance. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed GCN-TFT consistently outperforms baseline models in condensation and mold detection as well as future risk forecasting. Across all tasks, the event-level F1 score ranges from 0.93 to 0.99, and the AUCPR consistently exceeds 0.89, indicating reliable event recognition and robust risk discrimination under realistic granary conditions. In the risk warning tasks, earlier warnings are achieved with an average lead time of 11.8 days for condensation and 11.5 days for mold, while low miss rates are maintained. Ablation studies confirm that mechanistic features primarily improve physically consistent decision stability, whereas the incorporation of known future information and the FAA branch substantially enhances forward-looking risk recognition. Interpretability analyses reveal that the dominant cues leveraged by the model align with grain storage mechanisms and practical supervision, thereby providing actionable evidence to support risk assessment and interventions.

title: Improving rice leaf area index monitoring accuracy via robot-integrated multi-sensors and meteorological data fusion with explainable machine learning
abstract: Accurate and non-destructive estimation of rice Leaf Area Index (LAI) is vital for crop growth assessment and yield prediction. Close-range, non-contact optical methods are commonly used for LAI monitoring. However, their accuracy is often limited by the platform, and most rely on single-source data prone to saturation effects and background interference. To overcome these limitations, this study develops a phenotyping robot–based multi-source, high-resolution data fusion approach for field-scale LAI monitoring. A phenotyping robot equipped with multispectral and high-resolution RGB cameras was used to collect vegetation indices, color indices, texture features, and canopy coverage extracted from high-resolution RGB imagery. These features were further combined with meteorological variables to build machine learning models. The Random Forest model achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.92, RMSE = 0.302). SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) was applied to interpret the model and quantify the importance of multispectral features, RGB-derived texture information, canopy coverage and meteorological factors. Canopy coverage, NDVI and Clgreen were identified as the key factors for improving model performance, and the complementary mechanism between canopy coverage and other features can alleviate the saturation effect in the high LAI stage. The results show that combining high-resolution remote sensing data from robots with meteorological data can effectively mitigate the saturation effect and soil background interference in LAI estimation, and significantly improve the accuracy of LAI estimation. This study provides a practical and scalable framework for field phenotyping and offers technical support for precise rice cultivation and smart agriculture.

title: Multimodal data fusion and attention-based deep learning for estimating winter wheat chlorophyll content
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf chlorophyll content is essential for monitoring crop growth and supporting precision agricultural management. The soil and plant analyzer development (SPAD) instrument readings represent the relative chlorophyll content (RCC) in leaves, a key indicator of photosynthetic capacity and physiological status in wheat. This study proposes a multimodal data fusion approach integrating unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived vegetation indices (VI) and texture features (TF) from multispectral imagery with short-term environmental time-series data collected from in-field meteorological and soil sensors to estimate winter wheat RCC. A self-attention deep neural network (SA-DNN) was developed to capture complex nonlinear relationships among multimodal inputs. Employing a multi-stage progressive feature selection strategy that combines Pearson and Spearman correlations, minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), eight optimal features were ultimately selected from VI and TF, together with indicators of short-term variability in environmental factors (EF). These features included OSAVI, NDRE, R-Mea, R-SEM, AH-std-7, DPT-std-7, SD-std-7, and pH-std-7. The SA-DNN model achieved the best estimation performance (R2 = 0.913, RMSE = 3.945), significantly outperforming traditional machine learning models such as XGBoost, random forest (RF), support vector regression (SVR), Adaboost, and partial least squares regression (PLSR). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further quantified the contributions of individual features, revealing that short-term (7-day) fluctuations in EF, particularly sunshine duration and air humidity, played a dominant role in regulating variations in RCC. Overall, this study demonstrates that the synergistic integration of multimodal data within an attention-based deep learning framework significantly augments the precision of winter wheat RCC estimation, providing a powerful tool for real-time crop growth monitoring and the optimization of precision agricultural management.

title: Deep learning identifies optimal single spectral band for non-destructive fresh weight estimation in cabbage: A novel paradigm for postharvest management technology
abstract:
Background
Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) systems offer rich spectral information for precision agriculture applications such as yield forecasting, but their high cost and complexity limit widespread adoption. The relationship spectral data complexity and prediction accuracy in non-destructive crop monitoring remains unclear, challenging the assumption that more complex spectral data inherently yields better predictions.
Methods
We developed a workflow integrating UAV-based HSI (150 bands) with deep learning to non-destructively estimate fresh weight of cabbage heads (n = 680). A two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) was deployed to identify the single most predictive wavelength through systematic feature extraction. Performance was benchmarked against 20 conventional multi-band vegetation indices (VIs).
Results
The CNN identified a single spectral band at 565.63 nm as the optimal predictor. A predictive model using only this single-band input achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.49 on an independent test set, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.99 kg and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.84 kg. This performance substantially surpassed the best-performing conventional multi-band VI (MCARI2, R2 = 0.34), representing a 44% improvement in explained variance using single-band data input.
Conclusion
This AI-driven approach autonomously distill HSI complexity into a single optimal wavelength that outperforms established multi-band indices. The findings provide a methodological framework for designing simplified, cost-effective spectral sensors for precision agriculture, potentially improving accessibility and scalability of crop monitoring technologies.

title: Generative AI empowers agricultural spectroscopy: Enhancing subsurface nutrient prediction with AE-DDIM and TimeLLM
abstract: Peanut roots serve as the primary organ for nutrient absorption and storage, and their spatio-temporal variations in nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) contents strongly influence yield formation. However, root samples are difficult to obtain due to their subterranean nature, and the complex nonlinear relationship between hyperspectral signals and nutrient contents limits the accuracy of traditional inversion models. This study proposed an AutoEncoder-Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model-Time-series Large Language Model (AE-DDIM-TimeLLM) framework that integrates physics-constrained generative augmentation with large-model semantic regression to generate peanut root hyperspectral data and achieve multi-element joint prediction across growth stages. In the AE stage, physical priors, such as reflectance range, band-group smoothness, and spectral coherence were embedded to ensure physically consistent latent representations. In the DDIM stage, Wavelength Positional Encoding (WPE), Bandwise Attention, and Dual-Domain block were introduced to further improve spectral structural fidelity. As a result, the generated spectra achieved superior performance in PSNR, MRAE, RMSE, and Valley-Corr, surpassing conventional generative models in both structural accuracy and physical realism. Based on the generated data, the TimeLLM model employed feature-driven prompt reconstruction to jointly predict N, P, and K contents across growth stages, yielding a 5–12% increase in Rp2 and approximately 20% reduction in RMSEp. Moreover, the study identified an optimal augmentation ratio that maximized model generalization without overfitting. These results demonstrate that integrating spectral physical constraints with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) and semantic spectral-element modeling provides a promising pathway for accurate subsurface nutrient inversion, offering new data-driven insights for precision fertilization and nutrient management in peanut cultivation.

title: A filtering-based reinforcement learning strategy for adaptive task routing in multi-actuator robotic weeding
abstract: Robotic laser weeding offers high precision and environmental sustainability, making it a promising alternative to chemical herbicides. However, existing multi-actuator robotic systems struggle to balance planning latency, workload distribution, and actuator–chassis coordination, particularly under limited computational capacity and dynamic target distributions during chassis motion. To address these challenges, this paper presents ChronoRouteMaster (CRM), a dynamic task planning and collaboration strategy tailored for robotic multi-gimbal laser weeding. CRM formulates traversal planning as a variant of the Dynamic Vehicle Routing Problem, where the degree of dynamism is governed by chassis motion. The proposed method utilizes dynamic subspace partitioning with a filtering mechanism based on the penalty function, enabling sequential optimization of unassigned tasks. A reinforcement learning-trained agent adaptively allocates penalties and controls chassis motion according to real-time task distribution, improving both workload balance and motion coordination. Experimental results show that CRM achieves an average time of 0.93 s per actuator per weeding and a success rate of 92.7%, representing a 30% efficiency improvement over the traditional intermittence strategy. Beyond laser weeding, CRM can be extended to robotic pollination, seeding, and spraying in dynamic multi-actuator scenarios.

title: Growth monitoring of rice based on UAV hyperspectral images and improved deep learning method: The QRCNN-BIGRU-MLLA network
abstract: In recent years, drone-based hyperspectral imaging has become a research hotspot for monitoring crop growth status. To address insufficient multi-source data fusion and low accuracy in rice growth monitoring, this study utilizes drone hyperspectral imagery to obtain vegetation indices (VIs) across four growth stages (tillering, jointing, heading, filling), subsequently fusing these VIs with IoT sensor data (temperature, humidity, light) to measure Leaf Area Index (LAI), Plant Nitrogen Content (PNC), and Aboveground Biomass (AGB). An improved deep learning architecture, the QRCNN-BIGRU-MLLA model, is proposed, integrating grouped 1D-CNN, bidirectional GRU temporal modeling, Mamba-like linear attention (MLLA) for cross-modal fusion, and quantile regression (QR) for uncertainty quantification. Experimental results show that the model achieves satisfactory performance compared with existing methods: validation of LAI R2 is 0.92 (27.7% improvement over SVM), RMSE is reduced by 23.5% compared to SVM; PNC reaches R2 of 0.89 (30.8% improvement over MLR), RMSE decreases by 58.1% and MAE by 25%; AGB attains a R2 of 0.91 (28.2% improvement over MLR), RMSE reduces by 30.2%. The 90% Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) reaches 93.7% (LAI), 92.8% (PNC), and 89.6% (AGB). The fusion of hyperspectral and environmental data via this enhanced deep learning approach substantially improves the accuracy and reliability of growth indicator monitoring, providing robust technical support for precision fertilization and water management in rice growing regions.

title: Real-time estimation of crop height and cutting width in rice combine harvesters using a deep learning–enhanced forward-looking vision system with dynamic camera attitude correction
abstract: Crop height and cutting width directly influence combine harvester feed rates, yet their measurement is often limited by separate sensing devices, fixed camera attitude assumptions, and small datasets, leading to high system complexity and reduced robustness. This study developed a deep learning–enhanced forward-looking vision system that employs a depth camera to capture synchronized depth and color images ahead of the combine harvester. For crop height estimation, depth and color data were fused through image alignment, color space conversion, global threshold segmentation, region-of-interest partitioning, and depth scaling. For cutting width estimation, images collected from three combine harvesters and five rice cultivars were used to train a YOLO11-SCC model enhanced with Swin Transformer, Context Aggregation, and CSP PConv Composite modules to detect harvesting boundaries. A dynamic camera attitude correction algorithm was proposed to compensate for pitch and roll variations. Validation results showed that dynamic correction reduced crop height errors by 43% in RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) and 47% in MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), and reduced cutting width errors by 24% in maximum error and 28% in MAE (Mean Absolute Error). The system achieved crop height RMSE of 0.59–1.78 cm and MAPE of 0.56–1.57%, and cutting width MAE of 2.04–4.20 cm with a maximum error of 2.19–7.61 cm. Field tests on three additional cultivars confirmed stable performance, with crop height RMSE of 1.41–1.79 cm and MAPE of 1.28–1.51%, and cutting width MAE of 2.18–2.71 cm and a maximum error of 4.23–5.32 cm. The proposed approach enables reliable, real-time capture of crop height and cutting width, providing a practical foundation for feed rate prediction and intelligent control in combine harvesting operations.

title: Nighttime apple harvesting image enhancement based on a global–local feature fusion diffusion model
abstract: Night-time harvesting is an important strategy for improving the efficiency of agricultural automation; however, image degradation under low-light conditions severely limits the perception accuracy of machine vision systems. In complex orchard environments, existing methods often suffer from detail loss and structural distortion, which makes it difficult to meet the requirements of high-precision operations. To address these limitations, this study proposes a generative diffusion model for image enhancement built on a U-Net backbone. A Transformer module is incorporated to capture global context, and a convolutional block attention module is used to strengthen features of fruit as well as branches and leaves. In addition, pyramid-based resolution sampling and a global color correction module are employed to balance detail recovery with color consistency. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a PSNR of 27.1144 dB and an SSIM of 0.8891 on a synthetic apple dataset. To further assess practical applicability, a comparative analysis is conducted using both a synthetic dataset and a real low-light dataset. The results indicate that the model offers measurable generalization to real scenes and provides improved detail reconstruction. After enhancement by the proposed model, the YOLOv13 detector’s mAP50–95 increases from 0.249 to 0.352. Overall, the proposed approach mitigates severe visual degradation under extreme lighting and provides technical support for all-day, high-precision automated agricultural operations.

title: Rigid-flexible coupling errors calibration based on machine learning for robotic harvesting arm in orchard
abstract: Apple harvesting robots provide a solution for the mechanized picking of fresh fruits, in which the dedicated apple picking robotic arms are the core components. However, various errors reduce the positioning accuracy and dynamic performance of the apple picking robotic arm, such as system errors from manufacturing tolerances and assembly errors, compliance errors caused by self-weight and load structures, and nonstructural errors caused by gear backlash. This paper introduces a novel method to improve the positioning accuracy of long-stroke picking robotic arm. A rigid-flexible coupling pose error model was established that integrates system error, self-weight and load compliance errors. Meanwhile, redundant parameters were eliminated to optimize the model through parameter error classification and analysis of the parameter error ratio. Moreover, a hybrid calibration method was proposed, combining iterative least squares method for parameter identification with a residual network for nonstructural error estimation. The identified errors were then compensated for using the error compensation method based on inverse kinematics. Simulation experiments demonstrated that the identification accuracy of the removing redundant parameters model was 93.478%. Compared with other traditional methods, the proposed method achieved the highest error estimation accuracy and the minimal calibration error. Physical experiment showed that the positioning error of the picking robotic arm decreased after calibration. The average position error and root mean square error of the picking robotic arm compensated by the proposed method were 0.278 and 0.202 mm, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error were 0.230° and 0.178°, respectively. Compared to before calibration, the average position error and root mean square error decreased by 95.221% and 95.182%, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error decreased by 94.080% and 93.541%, respectively. This work provides a methodological reference for error calibration in fruit picking robotic arms.

title: ToxiPlantNet: A UAV-based deep learning framework for toxic plant detection and quantitative analysis of spatiotemporal dynamics in grasslands
abstract: The rapid proliferation of toxic plants in natural grasslands suppresses forage growth, reduces ecosystem productivity, and destabilizes grassland functions. Effective management requires not only precise species identification but also a quantitative understanding of their fine-scale spatio-temporal dynamics. In this study, ToxiPlantNet is proposed as a pioneering UAV-based spatial analysis framework designed to facilitate a paradigm shift from basic individual-level detection to comprehensive ecological dynamic modeling. Using Euphorbia fischeriana as a representative species, the framework integrates high-precision deep learning with quantitative spatial indicators to characterize the fine-scale spatio-temporal evolution of toxic plant populations. TOXI-YOLO, an enhanced one-stage detector, serves as the core of the framework and incorporates a GhostDyna-RevCol (GD-RevCol) backbone, a ToxiFusion-Pyramid (TFP) neck, and a Dynamic Sparse Head (DS-Head) to strengthen multi-scale representation and contextual perception under heterogeneous grassland backgrounds. This architecture features a highly lightweight design (1.4 M parameters and 4.8 GFLOPs), providing a vital operational advantage for real-time deployment on edge devices during field monitoring. On the held-out test set, TOXI-YOLO achieves high-precision single-plant localization, with 89.3% precision, 85.2% recall, 91.1% mAP@0.5, and a mean geolocation error of 0.23 m. Based on the georeferenced detection results, key spatial indicators are introduced: the Spatial Aggregation Index (SAI) to quantify local clustering intensity, and the Detectable Density Change (DDC) to characterize spatio-temporal shifts between successive acquisitions. The application of these indicators identifies density hotspots and reveals the dynamic evolution of E. fischeriana populations. By coupling lightweight, high-precision detection with interpretable spatial metrics, ToxiPlantNet provides a robust and scalable framework for the dynamic assessment and sustainable agricultural and pastoral management of toxic plants in natural grassland ecosystems.

title: Cross-attention driven RGBD fusion in lightweight CNN–Transformer for real-time stress classification of seedlings during robotic transplanting
abstract: Timely selection of high-quality seedlings during robotic transplanting is crucial for ensuring optimal crop growth and productivity. However, accurate real-time seedling grading is technically challenging due to subtle visual differences among stress levels and the limited computational capacity of edge devices. To address this, we propose a lightweight RGBD (RGB and depth) multimodal framework for six-level stress classification of bell pepper seedlings. Our approach integrates a dual-stream CNN–Transformer architecture in which hierarchical cross-attention modules fuse color-texture cues from the RGB stream with depth-derived geometric cues at both shallow and deep feature layers. The compact tokenizer rapidly extracts multi-scale fused features, which allow transformer encoders to capture long-range dependencies, and an attention-pooling head produces class logits. To validate our algorithm, a dedicated dataset of 1537 paired RGBD images was collected with an oblique-view sensor during the pick-and-place cycle. Deployed on an edge-device, the network achieves an overall accuracy of 95.8 % and maintains 5.2 frames per second when integrated into the parallel transplant-control pipeline. Ablation studies reveal that effective fusion of RGBD channel can improve accuracy by 4.9 % over RGB-only baseline model, which supports the effectiveness of the modality-aware design. This study integrates RGBD imaging with an edge-ready hybrid network to provide a practical tool for automated seedling transplanting and an effective solution for multimodal perception in precision agriculture.

title: Integrating plant physiology with deep learning for fresh weight prediction across lettuce growth cycles
abstract: Crops exhibit substantial phenotypic variation throughout their growth cycles, making accurate fresh weight estimation challenging, particularly during early seedling stages when morphological features are limited. This study proposes a unified framework that integrates plant physiological knowledge with deep learning to improve fresh weight prediction across the entire growth cycle. The framework utilizes RGB-D canopy images and incorporates a biologically constrained loss function derived from allometric scaling relationships between canopy area and biomass. To enhance prediction robustness across different growth stages, three adaptive strategies are introduced, including regional weight indexing, error sensitivity adjustment, and micro-sample weight amplification. These mechanisms improve the model’s ability to handle difficult samples at early growth stages while maintaining accurate predictions during later developmental phases. Experiments conducted over complete growth cycles demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving an acceptable prediction rate of 92.96% within a ± 10% error range. The proposed framework improves fresh weight prediction accuracy across growth stages while particularly enhancing performance during early seedling stages, providing a reliable solution for crop phenotyping, automated plant factories, and precision agriculture applications.

title: TARAG: A time-aware retrieval-augmented generation framework for supporting precision crop pest and disease management through large language models
abstract: Plant diseases and pests cause significant annual crop losses, severely threatening global food security. To mitigate crop losses, large language models (LLMs) demonstrate the ability to alleviate challenges in accessing precise farming support by acting as intelligent assistants that provide farmers with timely and precise decision support services. However, existing efforts still fall short in precision due to the neglect of time-sensitive nature in agricultural practices. They implicitly treat domain knowledge as time-irrelevant, ignoring the impact of crop phenology and pest life stages in their generated recommendations. To address this challenge, we propose a Time-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (TARAG), comprising a time-aware knowledge base construction module, a hybrid retrieval module, and a time-based generation module to provide precise pest management suggestions. Firstly, the time-aware knowledge base construction module constructs a time-annotated knowledge base from unstructured documents to provide supplementary agricultural knowledge. Secondly, the hybrid retrieval module performs coarse-grained sparse retrieval to ensure relevance, with a time-sensitive re-ranking stage that refines the results to achieve both semantic relevance retrieval and time alignment with user queries. Finally, the time-aware generation module leverages the top-k retrieved documents and an instruction prompt to produce the final suggestion. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we contribute TAQA, the first bilingual, time-annotated agricultural question-answering dataset. Experiments demonstrate that TARAG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art RAG frameworks in retrieval precision and suggestion quality, with 99.14% retrieval recall and an F1 score of 66.85% for generated suggestions. The implementation and datasets for this work are available in https://github.com/lee-hash1/agri_rag.

title: Leaf area extraction framework: Transformer-based segmentation and geometric-based completion approaches for accurate extraction of field maize leaf area from point clouds
abstract: The accurate determination of the maize leaf area is crucial for precision agriculture and yield optimization. Three-dimensional point-cloud technology provides a non-destructive and efficient alternative to traditional methods, which are often inefficient and inaccurate. This study aims to develop a robust field-compatible framework for maize leaf area extraction. It focuses on two key challenges: interference from environmental factors, such as strong sunlight, during point-cloud collection, and the mutual occlusion of leaves under complex field conditions. To address the first challenge, we propose a structured light-based point-cloud acquisition system that is optimized to minimize sunlight interference, thus enabling high-fidelity data collection in outdoor environments. We then utilize a Transformer-enhanced semantic segmentation network to isolate individual leaves accurately, achieving high precision across key evaluation metrics, including the precision, recall, F1-score, and intersection over union. The leaf area is subsequently calculated through triangulation. Our analysis revealed distinct performance variations between the vegetative and reproductive growth phases. While the framework demonstrated exceptional accuracy during the early stages, the performance declined significantly during the tasselling-to-maturity phase, owing to increased leaf occlusion and geometric complexity. To address this issue, we introduce two novel geometric processing algorithms: leaf contour completion and leaf body completion. These algorithms collectively enhance the accuracy, and the improvement effect becomes more significant as the point-cloud loss intensifies. Consequently, the most pronounced improvements are observed in the later growth stages. This work contributes to precision agriculture by establishing a growth-stage-adaptive leaf area extraction framework that aligns technical innovations with agronomic needs.

title: In situ orange soluble solids content estimation based on hyperspectral imaging and transformer
abstract: The in-field estimation of the oranges’ soluble solids content (SSC) using hyperspectral imaging(HSI) holds significant importance in facilitating the implementation of automated agricultural robots for selective harvesting operations and ensure the fruit quality. However, HSI analysis primarily utilizes the conventional machine learning approaches trained on small-scale datasets, which restricts prediction accuracy and generalization capability. Additionally, the high cost of hyperspectral cameras greatly hampers their widespread application in agricultural scenarios. This study proposed the utilization of transformer-based models for HSI analysis to SSC of oranges. Moreover, it explored the use of spectral reconstruction algorithms in reconstructing hyperspectral images from RGB images. A dataset for citrus was first established, which comprises 1536 samples; each sample includes a hyperspectral image, a RGB image and its corresponding SSC value, collected the growth of citrus from early maturity to late harvest across various field conditions. The hyperspectral images without reflectance calibration and dimensional reduction were utilized as input for training the transformer-based model for SSC prediction. The proposed transformer-based SSC prediction model on raw data demonstrated 14.8% better performance than PLS in terms of R2 (0.70 vs. 0.61), 11.7% better in terms of RMSE (0.83°Brix vs. 0.94°Brix). To validate the effectiveness of spectral reconstruction models, reconstructed hyperspectral images from RGB images are used for estimating the SSC of oranges. Their SSC prediction results consistently outperformed those derived from the corresponding RGB images, whether these were rendered from hyperspectral images (R2 = 0.64 vs. 0.56) or captured using a smartphone RGB sensor (R2 = 0.48 vs. 0.42). These results indicated that the capabilities of deep learning technologies to reduce costs and enhance accuracy, which can help promote the widespread application of automated selective harvesting operations and ripeness monitoring in agricultural scenarios.

title: FENE: Fish-conditioned Expert Network using deep learning for multi-species marine distribution modeling
abstract: Accurate species distribution modeling (SDM) is essential for sustainable fisheries management and marine ecosystem conservation, particularly in environmentally heterogeneous regions such as the Mediterranean Sea. While existing SDM approaches capture aspects of non-linear relationships, spatial variability, or uncertainty, relatively few jointly model species-specific responses, geospatial structure, and predictive uncertainty within a unified multi-species framework. In this study, we propose FENE (Fish-conditioned Expert Network), a deep learning architecture that integrates environmental predictors, spatial information, and species identity for multi-species SDM. The framework combines species-conditioned feature modulation, continuous spatial encoding, and a mixture-of-experts prediction mechanism to capture heterogeneous ecological responses while producing probabilistic outputs. We evaluate the model on a public Mediterranean dataset comprising eight commercially important pelagic fish species. FENE achieves strong predictive performance (RMSE = 0.071, R2 = 0.952), outperforming commonly used machine learning baselines, including tree-based and kernel-based methods, under the same evaluation setting. Performance further improves with feature selection (RMSE = 0.060, R2 = 0.968), indicating robustness to high-dimensional environmental inputs. Beyond predictive accuracy, the model enables species-specific interpretation via feature-attribution analysis and produces spatially explicit uncertainty estimates. Higher uncertainty is observed in ecotonal and data-sparse regions, indicating reduced model confidence under environmental variability. These results demonstrate that FENE can jointly model species-specific responses and quantify predictive uncertainty within a multi-species SDM setting.

title: Mango Expert: a harvest-optimizing wearable decision support system based on multimodal optoelectronic fusion and graph temporal neural networks
abstract: As a tropical cash crop, the precise quality assessment of mangoes directly determines optimal harvest timing and supply chain efficiency. Premature harvesting results in insufficient flavor, while delayed harvesting leads to spoilage and decay. Traditional manual or static imaging methods suffer from high subjectivity and inability to capture the dynamic ripening process. To address this, we propose Mango Expert, an intelligent decision-support system integrating visible/near-infrared spectroscopy and impedance sensing via a flexible optoelectronic sensor network. The system combines EfficientNet-B1 for image feature extraction, a BiLSTM model with positional encoding for temporal modeling, and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to dynamically model inter-fruit relationships. By fusing spectral and impedance data, our approach overcomes limitations of unimodal methods, achieving 98.54% classification accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Key innovations include adaptive graph construction and time-continuous batch sampling, which preserve biological correlations and enhance robustness. Deployed in real-world harvesting, the system reduces labor costs by 60% and increases premium fruit value by 20–30%. The system developed in this study demonstrates clear application value in precision fruit harvesting, providing a key tool for the fine-grained harvest decision-making in smart agriculture.

title: Data-driven optimization of CO2 regulation intervals in controlled environment agriculture
abstract: Precision carbon regulation in controlled environment agriculture (CEA) is essential for promoting crop growth and enhancing energy use efficiency. However, existing CO2 regulation strategies are predominantly based on fixed setpoints or empirically defined intervals, which fail to adequately capture nonlinear crop physiological responses, environmental interactions, and multiobjective trade-offs under practical conditions. To address these issues, this study formulates a data-driven CO2 regulation optimization problem and proposes a hybrid optimization framework. First, a support vector regression-based photosynthetic rate (Pn) model is developed to provide quantitative feedback for regulation design. Second, a biologically-informed constrained non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is designed to identify feasible CO2 regulation intervals under physiological and operational constraints, improving both convergence efficiency and solution quality. Third, a hybrid decision-making module integrates the best-worst method for weight determination and the measurement of alternatives and ranking according to compromise solution method for solution ranking, enabling robust selection from the Pareto-optimal set. Comprehensive comparative and ablation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Compared with Pn maximum strategies, the proposed method reduced Pn by 17.48% while significantly improving CO2 utilization efficiency (CUE) by 42.16%. It also achieves comparable Pn and CUE with lower CO2 input and fewer device activations than threshold-based strategies. Real-world validation shows reductions of over 40% in CO2 supplementation frequency and 16% in total CO2 dosage. Additional experiments on cucumber and eggplant further demonstrate the transferability of the proposed framework across crop types. Overall, this study provides an extensible solution for sustainable CO2 management in CEA systems.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable EEG-based deep learning framework for estrus detection in dairy cows
abstract: Electroencephalographic (EEG) signals exhibit stable and reproducible differences between estrus and non-estrus dairy cows, indicating that central nervous system activity reflects estrus-related regulation beyond external behavioral expression. Analysis across multiple EEG domains shows that estrus-associated neural modulation involves coordinated changes across frequency bands and recording channels and remains identifiable under varying behavioral conditions. Using multi-channel EEG recordings collected from 90 dairy cows, estrus detection was evaluated in a cross-subject evaluation, in which training and testing were conducted on data from different individuals. Under this evaluation protocol, the EEG-based approach achieved an accuracy of 92.7 ± 1.5%, an area under the curve of 94.0 ± 1.4%, a sensitivity of 94.1 ± 1.4%, and a specificity of 95.4 ± 1.3%, demonstrating robust discrimination across individuals rather than reliance on individual-specific neural patterns. Comparative model evaluation under unified experimental conditions indicates that appropriate feature representation and modeling strategies consistently capture estrus-related neural patterns. Attention-based interpretability analysis further reveals that EEG frequency bands contribute unequally to estrus discrimination, with low-frequency components, particularly the delta band, exhibiting the highest and most stable contribution across behavioral conditions. These results support EEG as a physiologically meaningful and interpretable information source for cross-individual estrus detection in dairy cows.

title: Vineyard Yield Prediction using Radar Images and a Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Predicting vineyard yield before harvest is valuable for optimizing logistics, resource allocation, and grape quality management. Traditional yield estimation methods based on manual sampling or optical imaging often suffer from high uncertainty due to occlusions, illumination variability, and grape bunch concealment. In this paper, we propose a deep learning–based approach for vineyard yield prediction using proximal millimeter-wave radar images, which are inherently robust to lighting conditions and capable of detecting partially or fully hidden grapes. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to learn the relevant feature representation directly from radar images acquired between consecutive vineyard posts and to estimate grape weight through end-to-end regression. However, radar images are affected by clutter, i.e., unwanted echoes that degrade prediction accuracy, particularly in low-yield scenarios. To address this issue, we introduce a novel graphical deep learning method (G_DL) based on image pair averaging, which reduces the influence of clutter during training and inference. The proposed method was validated using radar datasets collected over four growing seasons (2019–2022). The baseline CNN model achieved validation errors of approximately 15–18% (R2 ≈ 0.64), while the proposed G_DL method reduced the prediction error to approximately 8%. The results demonstrate that combining radar imaging with the proposed graphical deep learning strategy significantly improves yield prediction accuracy and robustness under the studied vineyard conditions, where multiple grape varieties coexist without requiring variety-specific calibration. This approach shows strong potential for integration into precision viticulture systems to support pre-harvest operational decisions related to logistics, workforce planning, and yield management.

title: Improved causal attention mechanism and semi-supervised learning integrated deep learning model for blueberry ripeness detection
abstract: The high nutritional value of blueberry has driven production scale expansion, with efficient harvesting and precision management becoming key for industrial upgrading—blueberry ripeness grading is its core link. Mainstream fruit ripeness detection methods use ordinary or hyperspectral images as data foundations, relying on machine learning-based computer vision. However, they have two critical limitations: only focusing on data correlation while overlooking causality, failing to unearth the intrinsic links between fruit growth and ripeness and thus resulting in misjudgments in complex scenarios; and poor cost and deployment adaptability, relying on large-scale manual annotations and high equipment costs, which cannot meet low-cost portable field needs. To address these, this study takes YOLO11 as the baseline and proposes YOLO11-WBO, a semi-supervised lightweight model for blueberry ripeness grading.
