Structurally, it integrates three customized modules: C2PSA_BCA includes causal attention and blueberry-specific features to enhance key information representation; C3k2_WT adopts wavelet convolution for accurate multi-scale feature extraction; C3k2_OREPA uses “multi-branch optimization during training and single convolution deployment during inference” to improve feature efficiency. A semi-supervised learning framework reduces reliance on large annotated data. Experiments on a blueberry dataset show YOLO11-WBO outperforms the original YOLO11n by 3.3 % in Precision and 4.6 % in mAP@50:95, maintains 8.33 ms per-image inference speed, and cuts annotation effort by 63 %. This work provides a low-annotation, low-cost, high-robustness solution for blueberry ripeness grading, with significant practical value and broad promotion prospects.

title: A deep learning-based adaptive control system for intelligent drying of horticultural flowers: A novel approach to reducing postharvest losses
abstract: Significant postharvest losses during the drying of horticultural flowers pose a threat to the stability and economic viability of their industrial supply chains. Existing drying processes, which rely on static, fixed-parameter settings, fail to effectively balance drying efficiency with final product quality, thereby exacerbating this challenge. This study developed and validated a deep learning-based adaptive control system for hot-air drying using chrysanthemums as a representative model, which enables dynamic regulation of drying parameters based on real-time monitoring of appearance quality. For the accurate online assessment of appearance quality, this proposed system incorporated a Spatial Interaction-Aware Segmentation (SIA-S) network. Trained on a dataset of 6889 images (partitioned into a 7:2:1 ratio for training, validation, and testing), the network achieved an mIoU of 96.20% and a Precision of 97.85%. These quantified appearance quality indicators were then fused with sensor-derived drying rates to train a Temporal Feature-Enhanced LSTM (TFE-LSTM), which outperformed standard baseline models (CNN, LSTM, and CNN-LSTM) in predicting quality evolution trajectories (R2 > 0.9970). Based on real-time predictions, the adaptive control system dynamically regulated drying parameters at 30-min intervals, yielding an optimized 300-min drying process. The resulting optimal trajectory consisted of a temperature sequence of [40, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 50, 60, 50, 60] oC and an air velocity sequence of [1.2, 2.8, 2.8, 2.8, 2.8, 2.8, 2.0, 2.8, 2.0, 2.8] m/s. Experimental results showed that compared to fixed-parameter drying, the proposed strategy significantly (p < 0.05) reduced drying time, achieved energy savings of up to 36.73%, improved the color profile (higher lightness and lower yellow index), inhibited shrinkage (a minimum shrinkage ratio of 0.51), and increased retention of marker phenolic compounds. A comprehensive evaluation score of 0.65 further validated the system’s effectiveness. Overall, this adaptive control system provides a theoretical and technical foundation for the intelligent drying of horticultural flowers.

title: The orchard tractor navigation method based on UAV photogrammetry combined with safety reinforcement learning
abstract: Autonomous navigation for orchard tractors faces significant challenges in robust path planning and reliable operation in unstructured orchard environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes a human-robot collaborative driving navigation method for tractors, based on UAV photogrammetry and safe reinforcement learning. First, rapid semantic segmentation and global path planning are achieved using UAV photogrammetry and an Attention U-Net model. Second, a composite control strategy utilizing APF-MPC-Safe RL-HIL is designed. This approach incorporates an Artificial Potential Field (APF) into Model Predictive Control (MPC) to provide safety-aware baseline path tracking. It further introduces the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm to learn residual steering corrections for the MPC controller in complex terrain conditions. Additionally, a Human-in-the-Loop (HIL) safety intervention mechanism is introduced to provide expert corrective actions during unsafe exploration, thereby accelerating reinforcement learning convergence and improving operational safety during the initial exploration phase. The system underwent pre-training and parameter iteration within a Gazebo simulation environment, followed by deployment and validation in real-world orchard scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits robustness in typical operations, maintaining an average lateral deviation within 0.13 m. This study provides a practical solution for the rapid deployment of autonomous navigation in orchard environments, with both theoretical significance and practical engineering value.

title: Low-light image enhancement with shallow diffusion model based on collaborative sampling
abstract: Complex lighting conditions pose significant challenges to high-level fruit detection in robotic harvesting systems, because lighting issues cause images to suffer from a degradation in detail. Deep learning models have been widely adopted for image enhancement, among which diffusion models have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in recovering high-quality images. However, diffusion models are often constrained by time-consuming and excessive computational resource consumption owing to their pixel-level iterative process. To address these constraints, we propose a novel shallow diffusion model for image enhancement that performs in the frequency-domain measurements instead of the image space via collaborative sampling. The shallow diffusion mechanism accelerates the inference time by reducing the number of denoising steps. Moreover, we optimized the refined reconstruction process to improve image quality. Extensive experiments on mango datasets demonstrated that the proposed method achieved superior performance and efficiency. Our research addresses the challenge of poor visual imaging quality caused by variable lighting conditions in agriculture. This advancement improves downstream tasks, such as target recognition, and can be extended to intelligent agricultural vision applications.

title: Improved estimation of daily maize evapotranspiration and its components by hybridizing long short-term memory with convolutional neural network and transformer neural network
abstract: Crop evapotranspiration (ET) and its partitioning into soil evaporation (E) and plant transpiration (T) are essential for understanding surface-atmosphere interaction, designing irrigation scheduling, and managing water resources. Nevertheless, direct measurement of ET and its components is time-consuming, labor-intensive and costly, which highlights the imperative of establishing accurate estimation models with readily available data. Two novel hybrid deep learning models, i.e. convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and transformer neural network-LSTM (Transformer-LSTM) models were proposed to estimate daily maize ET and its partitioning (especially E), and their performances were compared with SVM, XGBoost, DNN and standalone LSTM models. Meteorological (reference crop evapotranspiration, ET0), soil (soil water content, SWC; soil temperature, Ts) and crop (leaf area index, LAI; plant height, H) variables were grouped into eight input combinations to explore their effects on estimation accuracy. The percentage of the data used for training and testing was 4:1. The results showed that the inclusion of Ts and H can effectively enhance the model’s accuracy in estimating daily ET and its components, and it is necessary to take all variables into account while using the machine learning models to estimate daily maize ET and its components. The Transformer-LSTM exhibited satisfactory accuracy (R2 ≥ 0.841 and NRMSE ≤ 0.326) with only ET0. Crop variables, especially LAI, exerted greater influence than soil variables. The Transformer-LSTM model slightly outperformed CNN-LSTM, followed by LSTM, DNN, SVM and XGBoost almost under all input combinations, showing the best estimation accuracy of R2 = 0.894, MAE = 0.166 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.217 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.266, and |MBE| = 0.000 mm d−1 for E estimation with ET0, LAI and H, R2 = 0.955, MAE = 0.221 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.296 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.147, and |MBE| = 0.017 mm d−1 for T estimation and R2 = 0.955, MAE = 0.287 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.379 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.134, and |MBE| = 0.021 mm d−1 for ET estimation with all variables. This study highlighted the potential of hybrid LSTM models and the importance of meteorological and crop variables for accurate estimation of ET and its components in maize fields.

title: PB-DETR: multi-behaviour recognition of group-housed pigs with adaptive liquid neural network encoder and dynamic supervision
abstract: The behavioural recognition of group-housed pigs constitutes a fundamental pillar for animal health monitoring and precision feeding within the realm of intelligent husbandry. However, environmental complexities—including fluctuating illumination, occlusion interference, and significant scale variations across the full growth cycle—severely constrain the generalisation capabilities of existing models. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PB-DETR, featuring a redesigned encoder and loss function within the framework. Inspired by time series, we innovatively propose an adaptive liquid time constant enhancement (ALTE) network in image data, integrate the liquid time constant (LTC) mechanism into the Transformer-based encoder, and introduce a dynamic enhancement module to exploit the temporal modelling capabilities of LTC. By projecting 2D image features into a characteristic evolution space and solving ordinary differential equations (ODEs) inspired by biologically motivated neural dynamics, this module simulates the continuous non-linear evolution of features along the spatial dimension, thereby effectively alleviating the model’s dependence on background information. Building upon this enhanced representation, a Nexus Pyramid Network (NPN) is further constructed to resolve scale inconsistencies across feature maps. By employing a two-stage iterative refinement strategy and focal feature units with dilated receptive fields, the NPN establishes bidirectional semantic interaction pathways across multi-scale features, ensuring robust and accurate spatial perception of pigs across varying sizes. With respect to the loss function, a Dynamic Quality Boost Loss (DQBL) is proposed, which adopts an exponential moving average (EMA)-based dynamic benchmark to evaluate the relative quality of predictions with respect to the model’s current performance, and adaptively adjusts prediction weights to guide continuous optimisation. To rigorously evaluate the reliability of the model’s generalisation, this study developed a large-scale dataset encompassing four typical husbandry environments. Beyond performance comparisons on standard validation sets, independent cross-dataset inference tests were conducted across four heterogeneous scenarios. The results demonstrate that PB-DETR outperforms state-of-the-art methods across key metrics, achieving an mAP of 0.893 while maintaining low computational overhead, with 14.58 M parameters and 49.12 GFLOPs. This validates its practical utility and potential for deployment in complex farming scenarios.

title: Early and stage-specific detection of Magnaporthe oryzae on rice leaves using hyperspectral imaging and feature-based machine learning
abstract: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, is a major threat to rice production, initiating subtle biochemical and structural changes in rice tissues before visible symptoms develop. This study applied hyperspectral imaging combined with Fisher discriminant feature selection and machine learning to monitor rice blast progression over six consecutive days following pathogen inoculation. Based on symptom development, the infection process was categorized into three stages: (i) a latent asymptomatic stage (Days 1–2), during which plants remained visually indistinguishable from healthy controls; (ii) a very early symptomatic transition stage (Day 3), characterized by faint chlorosis, minor pigment non-uniformity, and microscopic pre-lesion points; and (iii) a progressive symptomatic stage (Days 4–6), marked by the gradual development of visible chlorotic halos and well-defined elliptical necrotic lesions. Feature importance analysis revealed that texture descriptors (energy, entropy, correlation, RMS, variance) were the most sensitive indicators during the latent stage, capturing oxidative stress and early chlorophyll destabilization primarily within the green reflectance region (430–580 nm). Descriptive statistical features (maximum, mean, median) became increasingly relevant during the early symptomatic phase (460–660 nm), reflecting progressive pigment degradation and water-content reduction. Shape-based descriptors (leaf area, perimeter, major/minor axis, circularity) were most informative in advanced stages (850–950 nm), when visible lesions expanded and tissue structure deteriorated. During the latent phase (Days 1–2), when no visual symptoms were present, RF achieved detection accuracies of 34.18% and 67.50% on Days 1 and 2, respectively, compared with SVM (25.80%, 54.50%), k-NN (20.10%, 43.30%), and DT (18.40%, 35.90%). As the disease advanced and visible symptoms began to appear, RF detection accuracy increased to 90.06%-93.19% on Days 3–4 and 96.32%-100% on Days 5–6. Hyperspectral analysis further revealed progressive spectral divergence in key wavelength regions (430–470 nm, 540–580 nm, 610–660 nm, and 850–950 nm), enabling sensitive detection during latent and very early symptomatic stages before lesion development. These results demonstrate that the integration of texture, color, and shape features enables precise, stage-specific detection of rice blast from pre-symptomatic infection to advanced disease manifestation.

title: A deep reinforcement learning-guided memetic algorithm for multi-objective collaborative scheduling of agricultural weeding robot fleets
abstract: The rapid deployment of intelligent unmanned systems is accelerating the transformation of precision agriculture. However, achieving autonomous, energy-efficient, and workload-balanced collaboration among heterogeneous weeding robot fleets in large-scale and structurally complex farmlands remains challenging. This study addresses a multi-objective collaborative scheduling problem for agricultural weeding robot fleets, aiming to minimize total travel distance, total energy consumption, and workload imbalance among robots. The problem is NP-hard, and conventional evolutionary approaches often suffer from limited adaptability due to static operator usage in complex search environments. To overcome these limitations, a deep reinforcement learning-guided memetic algorithm (DRL-MA) is developed. A dueling double deep Q-network is embedded within a Pareto-based memetic framework, where operator selection is formulated as a Markov decision process to enable adaptive exploration–exploitation balance. The framework further incorporates task-priority-based encoding, feasibility-preserving decoding, and a multi-stage hybrid heuristic initialization strategy to enhance convergence and solution diversity. Extensive experiments on benchmark smart-farm scenarios and a real-farm case study demonstrate that DRL-MA outperforms representative evolutionary, reinforcement-learning-assisted, and recent learning-based baselines. In the benchmark experiments, DRL-MA improves the mean hypervolume by approximately 11.7% and reduces the mean inverted generational distance by approximately 64.2% compared with the strongest competing algorithm. In the real-farm case study, DRL-MA contributes 78.31% of the globally non-dominated solutions, indicating stronger overall Pareto competitiveness. Moreover, runtime and scalability analyses show that the proposed method remains computationally feasible as the problem scale increases. These results indicate that DRL-MA provides an effective, scalable, and practically applicable scheduling approach for collaborative weeding robot fleets in smart farming.

title: Accurate individual-tree aboveground biomass estimation via physics-guided machine learning on UAV-based LiDAR and multispectral data
abstract: Accurate estimation of individual-tree above-ground biomass (AGB) is critical for assessing carbon storage at fine-scale. Current methods are constrained because traditional approaches underuse structural information, and purely machine learning (ML) models often overfit and lack ecological plausibility with limited in-situ samples. To address the limitations, this study develops a physics-guided machine learning (PGML) method that synergistically infuses tree allometric equations with ML. The model utilizes structural and biophysical features derived from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) and multispectral data. Validation with in-situ measurements shows that the PGML model achieved high accuracy across three tree species (Larch, Mongolian Scots Pine, and Populus), with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.80, 0.87, and 0.88, and root mean square errors (RMSE) of 8.14 kg, 9.56 kg, and 17.67 kg, respectively. The model also maintained low physical inconsistency ratios (PIR: 9.3, 9.84, 10.85) and outperformed three traditional methods by 12% to 18% in accuracy. Cross-regional direct transfer of the PGML model achieved R2 values of 0.43–0.73 in new plots. The primary innovation of this work is the effective fusion of physical growth mechanisms with data-driven ML, which concurrently enhances the predictive accuracy, stability, and ecological interpretability of individual-tree AGB estimation in complex forest stands.

title: PlantDiff: A diffusion model for high-fidelity plant image generation with Discrete Wavelet Transform and Context-Augmented Cross Attention
abstract: In recent years, deep learning technologies have achieved remarkable progress in agricultural applications, yet their performance heavily relies on large-scale, high-quality datasets and still faces widespread challenges such as data scarcity and class imbalance. To address these issues, data augmentation methods, such as generative adversarial networks or diffusion models, can generate high-quality images, thereby alleviating the limitations caused by insufficient training data. However, several critical challenges persist in plant science: the generated images often lack fine details such as leaf textures and venation patterns, and exhibit structural anomalies like fused leaves or detached stems. These issues lead to discrepancies between the generated and real data distributions, thereby degrading downstream task performance. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel latent diffusion model framework, termed PlantDiff. First, we design an Attentive Wavelet Feature Fusion (AWFF) module to optimize perceptual compression in diffusion models by decomposing images into high-frequency details and low-frequency global information using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), and enhancing feature integration through an Attention Estimation(AE) and Dynamic Fusion(DF) mechanism, thereby significantly improving the preservation of high-frequency details. Second, we introduce a Context-Augmented Cross Attention (CACA) module into the denoising network. This module captures local stem-leaf relationships using depthwise separable convolutions and extracts global growth structural features through Enhanced Gated Channel Transformation (EGCT), ensuring generated plant morphologies align with natural growth patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline models in plant image generation and benefits downstream tasks, with ablation studies confirming its effectiveness. The code of this paper will be available at https://github.com/Chuanyu-Li/PlantDiff.

title: A trajectory prediction method for vibrating fruits based on the LSTM-DA-iTransformer fusion model
abstract: In the process of intelligent fruit harvesting, the vibrations caused by external disturbances significantly affect the robot’s ability to quickly grasp the fruit. Accurately predicting the trajectory of the vibrating fruit is crucial for efficient grasping. However, traditional trajectory prediction models often struggle to achieve an effective balance between dynamic adaptability and long-term sequence prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid model—LSTM-DA-iTransformer. The model utilizes LSTM to capture local temporal features and integrates a Differential Attention Mechanism (DA) module to dynamically optimize attention weights in real time, adapting to variations in the vibration amplitude of the fruit. Additionally, the iTransformer strengthens long-term sequence dependency modeling to effectively mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Moreover, to further improve the model’s prediction accuracy and performance, the dataset was feature-adjusted by replacing position features with the position increments between time steps and timestamp features with the time differences between time steps. This adjustment helps avoid the impact of large-scale position features on model training and accelerates model convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model delivers superior performance in long-term sequence prediction tasks spanning 3 to 5 s. Specifically, within the 4-second time window, the Average Displacement Error (ADE) registers at 1.5475 cm, representing reductions of 41.6 %, 30.2 %, and 43.3 % relative to the GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer models, respectively. In the 5-second time window, the Final Displacement Error (FDE) amounts to 2.2185 cm, marking a decrease of 22.7 % to 39.2 % compared with the baseline models, alongside a 33.8 % to 48.3 % reduction in the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Additionally, ablation experiments rigorously verify the essentiality of each integrated module; notably, the DA module yields a remarkable improvement in prediction accuracy under complex vibrational scenarios.

title: In-Season monitoring of rice phenology for massive germplasm resources using Explainable Machine learning and a Transformer CNN model
abstract: Timely, accurate, and intelligent monitoring of rice phenology is crucial for selecting germplasm resources of suitable phenology, but previous research on phenological estimation has been based primarily on a few major rice cultivars in large scale field, lacking numerous germplasm resources in small breeding plots. Consequently, we proposed an in-season phenology monitoring framework that first identifies the growth stage of each rice plot and then estimates the initiation dates of key phenological stages for massive germplasm resources. This study utilized UAV to acquire time series imagery of 3112 rice germplasm resources across eight ecological sites. The improved CNN-Vision Transformer combined model classified the phenological stages, and based on these results, vegetation indices (VIs) for different germplasm resources at various growth stages were calculated. Subsequently, a Bayesian random forest regression model estimated the initiation dates of key phenological stages, and its performance was validated using an independent dataset. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis assessed the contributions of different VIs to phenological stages. The results demonstrated that Re-ViTAE achieved an accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient) values of 93.59 %, 93.03 %, 93.15 %, 93.08 % and 91.84 %, correspondingly, superior to all other eleven CNN and Vision Transformer models. RMSE of estimated initiation dates was 3.9d, 4.7d, 4.5d, and 3.7d for jointing, heading, grain-filling, and maturity, respectively, and the independent data validation accuracy was 5.6d, 5.3d, 5.8d, and 5.0d, respectively. Compared with the traditional RF model, the Bayesian-optimized RF model reduced the RMSE by 1.2 d, 1.2 d, 1.0 d, and 1.6 d, respectively. SHAP analysis revealed that different VIs contributed unequally to the estimation of key rice phenological initiation dates. Specifically, MTCI, NDVI, OSAVI, and Clgreen contributed most to the estimation of jointing, heading, grain filling, and maturity, respectively. The results of this study enable the quantitative classification for growth stages and estimation of initiation dates for massive rice germplasm resources, providing technical support for breeding scientists and companies in the selection of superior germplasms.

title: MSSVT: Multi-branch spatial-spectral volumetric transformer for rice lodging segmentation with UAV multimodal fusion
abstract: Deep learning-based fine-grained segmentation of typhoon-induced rice lodging provides important support for high-precision disaster assessment using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. However, many existing unimodal, flat multimodal, or generic cross-modal segmentation methods process heterogeneous UAV-derived features without explicitly preserving the semantic relationships among feature groups, which may limit modality-specific representation and spatial-spectral interaction. To address this challenge, this study investigates structured UAV multimodal fusion by organizing RGB physical features and multispectral physiological signatures into a semantically grouped volumetric representation. A Multi-branch Spatial-Spectral Volumetric Transformer (MSSVT) is proposed for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation. MSSVT uses a Hybrid Volumetric-Planar Backbone (HVPB), in which the Volumetric Spatial-Spectral Backbone (VSSB) models inter-group spatial-spectral dependencies, while the Planar Spectral Backbones (PSB) preserve fine-grained intra-group attributes. Within VSSB, the Volumetric Hybrid Attention (VHA) module combines dynamic sparse routing and selective scanning to capture salient lodging regions and refine boundary details. A progressive feature fusion mechanism is further used to integrate band-compressed, adaptively modulated, and multimodal aggregated features. To support this study, a multimodal Volumetric Rice Lodging (VRL) dataset was constructed for the investigated typhoon-induced lodging area. The dataset organizes 55 heterogeneous channels spanning RGB, color, texture, structure, multispectral, and vegetation-index features into a structured volumetric representation. Extensive experiments on the VRL dataset demonstrate that MSSVT achieves 90.72 % mIoU, representing a 1.31 % improvement over the strongest competing method. The proposed model obtains class-wise IoU values of 97.59 %, 78.10 %, and 91.02 % for normal rice, mild lodging rice, and severe lodging rice, respectively, with the largest gain observed for mild lodging rice (+5.16 %). These results indicate the potential of structured UAV multimodal fusion for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation under the investigated typhoon-induced field scenario. Code is available at: https://github.com/AG-WDS/MSSVT.

title: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests using time-series X-ray imaging and deep learning
abstract: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests is critical for improving monitoring efficiency and optimizing control timing. However, because these insects remain concealed within tree trunks before emergence, conventional approaches cannot exploit empirically observed developmental dynamics, limiting both forecast reliability and temporal resolution. To address this, we developed a field-deployable, non-destructive forecasting framework that integrates portable X-ray radiography, deep learning-based life-stage discrimination, and developmental-lag mapping to predict adult emergence dynamics from concealed development. We acquired X-ray images of wood-boring pests inside infested logs and developed X-BorerStageNet, a lightweight two-class life-stage detector (larva vs. pupa-adult). X-BorerStageNet introduces two task-specific networks—a structure-preserving backbone, the Efficient Dual-Stream Fusion Network (EDSFNet), and a frequency-aware multi-scale encoder, the Spectral-Attentive Multi-Scale Fusion Network (SAMFNet)—comprising five novel modules in total. Within EDSFNet, the Anisotropic Pseudo-Shift Downsampling Module (APSDM) preserves directional structural cues during early downsampling, and the Dual-Stream Hierarchical Ghost Block (DSHGB) reduces redundancy via complementary parallel branches that jointly capture fine details and coarser context. Within SAMFNet, the Spectral-Enhanced MetaFormer Block (SEMFB) couples global attention with FFT-based spectral modulation to enhance pest contours while suppressing repetitive wood textures; the Progressive Hybrid Aggregation Module (PHAM) strengthens cross-scale integration through an anchor–refinement design; and Tri-Scale Focused Fusion (TSFF) fuses three adjacent feature scales to balance fine details with semantic context. The model achieves 66.3% AP50:95 and 92.8% AP50, exceeding the D-FINE-N baseline by 6.9 and 4.2 percentage points, respectively, with fewer parameters and fast inference. Applied to time-series X-ray monitoring of 9 infested logs, the framework recovered the pupation dynamics of 72 Anoplophora glabripennis individuals and translated them into emergence forecasts using a mean pupation-to-emergence interval of approximately 20 days. Predicted emergence dynamics closely matched observations at both 3-day (r = 0.913, WAPE = 0.278) and weekly (r = 0.972, WAPE = 0.167) scales, and accurately recovered key phenological landmarks, including emergence onset, peak timing, and the 10%, 50%, and 90% cumulative-emergence dates. This framework offers an effective and interpretable approach for forecasting wood-boring pest emergence dynamics, supporting early warning and timely control. Source code: https://github.com/bihaojie/X-BorerStageNet.

title: MaizeStereo: 2D Gaussian splatting-driven stereo foundation model for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) maize phenotyping is instrumental in capturing the spatial structural features essential for crop breeding and guiding agricultural practices. Among existing 3D sensing technologies, stereo vision has achieved remarkable progress in reconciling cost‑effectiveness, environmental robustness, and operational efficiency, owing to its inherent advantages as a passive sensing modality. However, its limited precision collectively impedes the broader application for organ-level phenotyping. Building on advancements in stereo vision propelled by supervised stereo matching paradigms and large-scale foundation models, this study proposes a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS)-driven stereo foundation model approach for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping (MaizeStereo), which capitalizes on the intrinsic generalization potential of stereo foundation models while enhancing the adaptability to field proximal sensing via domain-specific optimization. Field experiments were conducted using a custom binocular image acquisition system on 50 maize plants across five growth stages (V3, V5, V7, V12, R3). The proposed MaizeStereo framework addresses real-field scenarios by synthesizing a high-fidelity stereo matching dataset through an advanced multi-view 2DGS reconstruction method. Leveraging the dataset for supervision, an optimal module-freezing strategy is developed to fine-tune the stereo foundation model for domain-specific performance enhancement. Based on the resulting disparity predictions, the framework further implements organ-level phenotypic trait extraction. Evaluated results showed that the fine-tuned foundation model outperformed benchmark methods in stereo matching with a global end-point error (EPE) of 1.846 pixels and a D1 error of 6.806%, achieving only a marginal 5.55% EPE increase compared to full fine-tuning while reducing trainable parameters by 45.7%. For phenotypic trait extraction, the pipeline delivered high accuracy with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 3.822% for plant height, 3.432% for stem diameter, and 7.741% for leaf area. The corresponding coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.994, 0.952, and 0.986 respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method enables efficient and precise maize phenotyping in complex field conditions, providing a valuable tool for crop breeding and agricultural research.

title: Unsupervised keypoint detection for automated livestock phenotyping: A multi-species approach based on pre-trained foundation models
abstract: In the realm of precision livestock farming, the identification of keypoint in livestock is a crucial area of research. Traditional supervised learning approaches face challenges in adapting to the complexities of livestock environments, including varied poses, occlusions, and inter-species differences, due to their reliance on extensive annotated datasets. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces a novel unsupervised keypoint detection methodology grounded in pre-trained foundation models. Our innovative approach combines the strengths of Stable Diffusion (SD), known for its exceptional fine-grained texture perception, with DINOv2′s structural similarity representation. We employ a normalized weighted fusion strategy to seamlessly integrates these complementary features, enabling multi-scale semantic alignment. Additionally, we have developed a unique multi-template voting mechanism that utilizes Mean-Shift clustering and inverse-distance weighting, significantly enhancing both the accuracy and stability of keypoint detection. To support this research, we have compiled a comprehensive livestock dataset encompassing 2204 images horse (804), cattle (309), sheep (767), and pig (324). Our experimental analysis, conducted across these species, reveals a high average detection accuracy (91.21% for horses, 91.09% for cattle, 84.76% for sheep, and 93.78% for pig), using the PCK@0.05 metric, which outperforms the SOTA method by 3.07, 4.62, 11.19, and 3.10 percentage points (pp), respectively. The proposed method demonstrates robust cross-species generalization capabilities, effectively managing significant pose changes and non-rigid deformations. It offers a versatile and efficient solution for keypoint detection, applicable to automated body measurement or animal behavior analysis in precision livestock farming applications. For access to the code and dataset, please visit https://gitee.com/wbxue/keypoints.

title: XylemVision: A Knowledge-Distilled deep learning framework for High-Throughput quantification of root anatomy in peanut
abstract: Manually quantifying root anatomy from microscope images has been a major bottleneck in crop research. Deep learning can automate this process, but requires large, labeled datasets that are expensive to create. Newer foundation models, like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) or DINOv2, appear to offer a solution but struggle with specialized scientific images. Even after fine-tuning, these models still require precise prompts such as bounding boxes or points to specify what to segment. A common workaround is to use an object detector (like YOLO) to create these prompts, but this reintroduces the original challenge of needing extensive labeled data to train the detectors itself. To address this bottleneck, a knowledge distillation (KD) framework was developed to train object detectors with minimal labeled data. Initially, a large DINOv2 teacher model was used to pretrain student detectors (YOLO11 and RT-DETR) on unlabeled root images, transferring its rich visual feature representation capabilities without requiring any labels. This pretraining phase enabled the student models to extract high-level generalized spatial features of the root images. The pretrained student detectors were then fine-tuned using a small, labeled dataset to detect anatomical features including xylem, vascular bundles, and the total root. Finally, the resulting bounding boxes were passed to a SAM-integrated segmentation pipeline to produce precise, pixel-level masks for trait extraction. Together, these steps form XylemVision, a unified and data-efficient pipeline for xylem phenotyping that demonstrates accurate detection, segmentation, and trait extraction with limited labeled data. Results showed that the KD-pretrained YOLO11 model demonstrated superior detection performance (0.922 mAP50–95) compared to its supervised baseline (0.884) and maintained comparable accuracy (0.917 mAP50–95) even when the labeled dataset was reduced by 25 %-75 %. By leveraging these precise bounding boxes as prompts, the SAM-based segmentation pipeline proved highly effective, achieving mean Intersection over Union (IoU) scores of 0.85–0.95 across all anatomical traits substantially outperforming YOLO11′s built-in segmentation module, which achieved only 0.10–0.58 IoU. Beyond these performance gains, the KD framework ensured strong transferability across species, successfully adapting to soybean root cross-sections without additional fine-tuning. Overall, this study develops a data-efficient framework that makes plant image analysis efficient and more accurate across different crops.

title: Concept-guided deep learning with UAV-satellite sample augmentation for daily 10 m crop AGB mapping
abstract: Aboveground biomass (AGB) is a fundamental variable for characterizing crop growth, yield potential, and agricultural carbon cycling. Achieving daily 10 m resolution crop AGB mapping at regional scales remains challenging. Here, a unified UAV-satellite framework is developed that integrates sample augmentation with concept-guided deep learning (DL) to enable high-resolution AGB mapping. UAV-derived canopy structural and spectral information is fused with satellite spectral and cumulative temporal features to generate virtual quadrats aligned with the Sentinel-2 pixel scale, thereby expanding the training dataset and mitigating the scarcity of field-based AGB measurements. These quadrats facilitate the development of a novel light-use-efficiency-guided Long Short-Term Memory model (LUE-LSTM), in which AGB is formulated as a cumulative state variable driven by photosynthetically active radiation, enforcing physiological constraints on AGB dynamics. Experiments in the Hetao Irrigation District demonstrate improved physical consistency of AGB temporal estimation, characterized by near-ideal temporal behavior (Normalized Time Variability Index, NTVI ≈ 1.0) and low deviation from realistic growth dynamics (Logistic Fitting Error, LFE < 60 g m⁻2). Cross-year and cross-region validation further demonstrates enhanced generalization, with R2 increasing from 0.741 to 0.815 and RRMSE decreasing from 0.220 to 0.185. Using the proposed framework, daily 10 m AGB maps were generated for 2019–2025, demonstrating strong potential for regional crop monitoring and agricultural carbon assessment.

title: Mitigating occlusion: a spatial-aware diffusion model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock
abstract: In livestock management, accurately capturing pose changes in quadrupedal livestock is crucial for disease prediction and behavioral analysis. However, due to inter-animal occlusion and obstructions from farming facilities, livestock in practical farming environments are often partially visible, making pose estimation highly challenging. Existing livestock-specific pose estimation models and transferred human pose estimation frameworks are limited by fixed structural constraints and insufficient discrimination of highly similar livestock features, resulting in inaccurate localization and missed detections of body keypoints under occlusion conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes SADPose, a Spatial-Aware Diffusion Model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock. The proposed framework combines noise-guided pose generation with hybrid-scale spatial constraints to improve robustness under severe occlusion. Specifically, a Hybrid-Scale Graph Convolutional Network is embedded into the diffusion framework to model local and global skeletal relationships. During the forward diffusion stage, the model constructs a feature space covering diverse livestock pose distributions, while the reverse denoising process progressively suppresses interference through multi-scale feature fusion, thereby reducing localization bias and missed detections of occluded keypoints. Experiments on two public datasets involving representative quadrupedal livestock species demonstrate that SADPose significantly outperforms existing methods in occlusion scenarios, improving keypoint localization accuracy and overall pose estimation performance in complex occlusion scenarios.

title: A conditional generative diffusion model enables joint retrieval of rice LAI and LCC
abstract: The critical growth stages of crops have short observation windows and are easily affected by environmental factors, which often limits the availability of field measurements for remote sensing inversion. This limitation is more pronounced in the synergistic inversion of leaf area index (LAI) and leaf chlorophyll content (LCC), where canopy structure and chlorophyll related traits may show similar spectral responses in the visible region. Such spectral overlap can lead to parameter confusion and estimation bias, highlighting the need for methods that can expand training samples while preserving the relationships among spectral features and crop traits. With recent advances in generative modeling, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) provides a potential solution by learning data distributions and generating synthetic samples that preserve these relationships. To address these issues, the study developed a conditional inversion for Remote Sensing model based on a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (CIRS-DDPM). In this model, LAI and LCC were embedded as continuous conditional variables and fused into the noise prediction network during reverse denoising, allowing the generated samples to better preserve the joint distribution among crop traits and remote sensing features. A Fully connected residual network for One-Dimensional Sequence Features (1D-ResMLP) was introduced as the backbone to improve noise prediction for tabular remote sensing data. The samples generated by CIRS-DDPM were compared with those generated by the Tabular Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Tab-DDPM) and PROSAIL. The results showed that CIRS-DDPM generated data had feature distributions highly consistent with measured samples. Models trained with CIRS-DDPM generated data also showed strong validation performance using real measurements. The one-dimensional residual network (1D-ResNet) model achieved R2 = 0.822, RMSE = 1.314, and MAE = 1.087 for LAI, and R2 = 0.735, RMSE = 10.397, and MAE = 8.251 for LCC. Compared with models trained using PROSAIL and Tab-DDPM generated data, the R2 values increased by 20.0 % and 57.0 % for LAI, and by 18.4 % and 31.8 % for LCC, respectively. These results indicate that CIRS-DDPM can improve data support for the synergistic inversion of LAI and LCC and provide an effective solution for data limited remote sensing modeling in agriculture.

title: Machine learning and physical modeling for water regulation at different phenological stages in efficient green paddy field production
abstract: Influencing both crop growth and the agro-ecological environment, water regulation is a key factor in agricultural production. However, few studies have considered the impact of dynamic field-scale blue and green water migration processes on farmland water regulation. A water–food–environment multi-objective collaborative optimization model incorporating stage-specific blue–green water migration processes was developed to establish the surrogate-modeling framework. Linear, multiplicative, and Transformer-based yield prediction models were compared, while an empirical drainage-based model served to represent the grey water footprint. To characterize stage-specific blue–green water partitioning and support irrigation optimization under different hydrological scenarios, the Transformer model was coupled with field water-dynamics simulation and the NSGA-II optimization algorithms. This framework allows the evaluation of stage-specific irrigation strategies that consider yield, blue water productivity, and drainage-related non-point source pollution risks. Using four hydrological-year types and six decision preferences, the framework was evaluated using field data from Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China, a representative rice-growing area in the lower Yangtze River region. The model generated coordinated trade-off solutions across the three objectives. Across the evaluated scenarios, the optimized solutions were associated with higher yield and blue water productivity and lower grey water footprint relative to baseline strategies, with average changes of approximately +30%, +176%, and −35%, respectively. The proposed framework functions primarily as a methodological template for site-specific offline irrigation decision support under different hydrological conditions. Although the quantitative optimization outcomes depend on local agro-hydrological conditions, the stage-based coupling framework and optimization workflow can be adapted to other rice-growing regions after local recalibration, validation, and scenario reconstruction.

title: Rapid detection of maize seed vigor via multi-branch interpretable deep learning integrated with multimodal data fusion optimized by environmental factors
abstract: Seed vigor is a core indicator of seed quality and field emergence performance. Existing rapid detection technologies perform poorly in field applications, neglecting the fusion of multimodal data and the effects of environmental factors on seedling emergence. Here, we collected 700 maize seed samples from diverse sources and acquired multimodal phenotypic data, including machine vision (MV), reflectance spectra (RS), and fluorescence spectra (FS). Seed vigor labels were obtained via a cold-soak germination test, with continuous recording of temperature and humidity during the process. Considering the complexity of seed vigor, we constructed a Four-branch Combined Dual-path Attention Mechanism Residual Network (FDRNet) to simultaneously classify seed vigor levels (low/high) and predict physiological indicators (fresh weight, germination energy, germination percentage). Furthermore, an AIseed Vigor software was developed, and its field performance for seed vigor prediction was verified via UAV remote sensing technology. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Multimodal data fusion (RS + FS) with FDRNet achieved the highest performance in seed vigor classification (Accuracy = 96.8%) and physiological prediction (Rp2 = 0.742/0.582/0.642). (2) SHAP interpretation revealed the spectral preferences of different physiological indicators: seed fresh weight was mainly determined by the 500 nm green band, while germination energy and germination percentage primarily depended on the 453 nm blue band, and combined with feature interaction analysis further verified the complex nonlinear relationships between spectral features and various seed physiological traits. (3) Incorporation of environmental factors reduced the RMSE of model by 5%–33%, with RHmax and Tstd showing greater effects on seedling emergence. (4) Emergence monitoring and vegetation index analysis based on remote sensing imagery confirmed that high-vigor seeds identified by AIseed Vigor exhibited significantly (P < 0.01) higher emergence rates and better early growth than low-vigor seeds, demonstrating robust transferability from laboratory to field.

title: A physics-guided hybrid framework for peanut nitrogen monitoring: Fusing radiative transfer physics with machine learning
abstract: Nitrogen, significantly affects peanut agricultural yield and development. Therefore, the effective detection of nitrogen is important for crop growth in the context of agricultural economics. However, conventional measurements of canopy nitrogen concentration are labor-intensive and time-consuming, limiting high-throughput monitoring. In this study, we developed a radiative transfer process-guided model for estimating nitrogen content in peanut canopy by integrating radiative transfer theory with empirical modeling approaches. A hyperspectral platform was utilized to monitor the canopy spectrum of 241 peanut accessions grown under four distinct environmental conditions. The peanuts canopy nitrogen content (CNC) monitoring model was constructed using spectrum data, combining a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets (WGAN) physiological parameter optimization with empirical models optimized via hyperparameter tuning. Compared to the conventional empirical model (R2 = 0.7544, mean squared error (MSE) = 13.0612), the proposed POSNH framework, a pre-trained LSTM network guided by optimized radiative transfer processes, attained significantly higher accuracy in CNC estimation (R2 = 0.8815, MSE = 5.8432). The POSNH model also exhibited exceptional robustness across data scarce which maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.8612) when the training set is reduced to 10 % and demonstrating generalization across independent environment yielding MSE values of 7.54, 5.07, 5.27, and 2.85 for Experiments 1–4. By leveraging Monte Carlo Dropout (MC Dropout) for simultaneous point estimation and uncertainty quantification, the model ensured high predictive reliability, with 95 % prediction intervals achieving 97.75 % empirical coverage. The POSNH demonstrates the potential of applying an optimized PROSAIL, hyperparameter search and modular training to improve the accuracy and cross-environment robustness of CNC prediction, providing a new approach for sustainable agricultural management.

title: Assessing social stress in Nile tilapia through AI behavioral analysis and biosensor integration
abstract: Measurements of stress responses in fish using a glucose biosensor make it possible to measure variations in blood glucose concentration – an indicator of stress in fish – as fluctuations in output current, even while the fish are allowed to swim freely. In this study, a new method was developed that integrates the glucose biosensor and AI-based posture estimation. Using the Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), variations in the concentration of stress indicator substances in the fish’s body were measured by the biosensor, and the fish’s behavior in the water tank was quantified using AI posture estimation. By integrating these datasets, we visualized the behavioral impacts of increase of biosensor current output induced by conspecific agonistic interactions. Conventional standalone physiological monitoring cannot characterize how an altered biosensor current output manifests behavioral change. When social interactions between two fish of different sizes were observed, the behavior of each individual differed. In addition, when focusing on the fish that was attacked violently by the dominant individual, it was confirmed that the range of behavior in the water tank changed in conjunction with the increase in biosensor current output. The results of this experiment showed the observational example of impact of aggressive social interactions on the stress levels and behavior of fish. The findings reported in this paper are based on a single aggressive pair and a single non-aggressive pair. Therefore, they primarily serve to demonstrate technical proof of concept.

title: EOL-DQN: An intelligent cutting decision of potato seed tubers based on improved deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Current intelligent seed-tuber cutting decisions mainly rely on preset geometric rules, which suffer from poor adaptability, single decision planning, insufficient multi-objective optimization, and poor dynamic response. There is an urgent need to develop an intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision that can adapt to complex seed-tuber shapes and bud-eye distribution, learn manual cutting experience, and balance bud-eye preservation with uniform tuber quality. Therefore, based on the principle of deep reinforcement learning, a DQN-based intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision was first proposed, which realizes seed-tuber cutting by designing the state space, cutter action space, exploration strategy and reward function. Pre-experiments show that the DQN decision has problems such as frequent collisions with bud-eye areas, disorderly cutting of multi-bud seed tubers, and low cutting qualification rate, leading to low seed-tuber utilization. To address this, this paper further carries out improvements from four aspects: multimodal feature extraction, cutting-direction optimization, reward-function design, and decision-network architecture, and proposes an EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision integrating agronomic seed-cutting requirements. First, a bud-eye protection mechanism was introduced to limit the exploration space of cutter actions and improve the agent’s active obstacle-avoidance ability; second, priority was given to selecting the action set that meets the cutting-direction constraints to cultivate the agent’s awareness of sequential decision-making, and the first-cut workspace was limited to the apical region of the seed tuber; third, a layered mixed reward function was designed with the introduction of tuber-area uniformity rewards to enhance bud-eye allocation capability and reduce the bud-free rate; finally, the decision-network architecture was improved to strengthen the multimodal-feature perception capability for seed-tuber contours and the spatial distribution of bud eyes. Experiments show that the cutting qualification rate (Drate) of the EOL-DQN decision algorithm reaches 90.17 %. Compared with DQN, DDQN, Dueling DQN, PERDQN, Noisy DQN, C51, QR-DQN and Rainbow DQN, the Drate of EOL-DQN is improved by 21.99, 16.02, 19.21, 15.65, 14.77, 22.83, 16.96 and 11.19 percentage points respectively. The single seed-tuber decision time of EOL-DQN is 0.034  s, which satisfies the real-time operation requirements of seed-tuber cutting. Platform cutting experiments demonstrate that EOL-DQN maintains a cutting qualification rate above 90 % for multiple mainstream seed-tuber cultivars, with no significant difference observed among cultivars (F = 0.0498, P > 0.05), and the cut tuber pieces can meet agronomic requirements. The EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision strategy proposed in this paper can provide effective technical support for intelligent potato seed-tuber cutting.

title: A non-destructive watermelon sweetness classification via vision transformer with cross-modal knowledge distillation
abstract: The quality of watermelon sweetness is essential to non-destructive classification that can be applied to the agricultural production process, but the current methods usually use expensive or destructive measures like spectrometry. This study presents a novel cross-modal knowledge distillation framework as a proof-of-concept for non-destructive fruit sweetness classification under constrained sample sizes. The framework consists of three main components, namely a pre-trained model of a teacher that processes both image and mineral concentration information, a vision transformer (ViT) that is a student component and takes images only, and a feature alignment network that links their respective intermediate representations. The student model learns the composite loss function that combines the classification loss, feature space alignment loss, and probabilistic distribution matching loss and hence maps the multimoded knowledge of the teacher to a unimodal one. The preliminary results of experiments show that the offered approach is superior to the traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. The provided framework reaches the rate of 94.5%, which is higher than the unimodal and multimodal baselines. Moreover, the suggested method can be applied to the empirical issue of implementing sweetness prediction in a resource-constrained environment because it needs standard imaging equipment.

title: NFGTN: A node-fusion graph transformer network for non-destructive estimation of glucoraphanin content in broccoli leaves using RGB-D imaging
abstract: Non-destructive estimation of crop biochemical traits is important for quality evaluation, precision cultivation, and nutritional breeding. As a major glucosinolate in broccoli, glucoraphanin (GRA) is an important indicator of nutritional and functional quality, yet its quantification still relies mainly on destructive chemical analysis. To address this limitation, this study proposes a node-fusion graph transformer network (NFGTN) for estimating GRA content in broccoli leaves using paired red–green–blue (RGB) images and aligned depth information, collectively referred to as RGB-D data. The proposed RGB-D framework integrates a visual backbone, offline graph construction, node-level multimodal fusion, and graph propagation with joint local–global readout within a unified regression architecture. Specifically, an offline graph is constructed to establish explicit correspondence between visual patch features and local plant regions, while a node fusion module is designed to adaptively integrate RGB appearance cues with depth-derived geometric descriptors. On this basis, graph propagation, weighted local pooling, and iterative global readout are employed to jointly model local structural dependencies and graph-level contextual information for final prediction. Experimental results under five-fold cross-validation show that the proposed NFGTN achieved the lowest RMSE of 0.1369, the highest R2 of 0.9232, and the highest RPD of 3.8239 among the compared RGB and RGB-D methods, with an MAE of 0.1098. Additional comparisons with hyperspectral models based on mean spectral representations showed that NFGTN achieved competitive sample-level GRA prediction performance under the present experimental setting.

title: Automated mating monitoring and occlusion-aware identity attribution in breeding chickens using multi-stage deep learning
abstract: Monitoring mating behavior can provide behavioral indicators relevant to reproductive management in poultry breeding. However, traditional manual observation is labor-intensive, subject to observer fatigue, and ill-suited to identifying specific individuals within dense flocks. To address these issues, this study develops a framework that attributes each mating event to persistently and uniquely identified individuals, thereby enabling per-individual and longitudinal mating-frequency analysis rather than flock- or event-level detection alone. Because the hens belong to a single breed, are viewed top-down, and are physically occluded by the rooster during mounting — conditions under which appearance-based re-identification fails — we introduce an occlusion-aware spatiotemporal matching algorithm that infers the occluded hen’s identity from interaction-induced disappearance, combining temporal gap detection, trajectory-based last-position estimation, and spatial validation within a dynamically defined interaction zone. A lightweight wearable vest-tag system, built around an occlusion-robust color–symbol code set, supplies the deterministic identity signal. Within the pipeline, YOLO11 performs rooster localization and tracking, and UniFormer performs spatiotemporal mating recognition. Experimental results from one 2.4 m × 1.2 m pen containing 44 Hy-Line Sonia hens and 4 roosters showed that UniFormer achieved the highest F1-score on each of the three independent test days. When predictions from the three days were pooled, UniFormer achieved an F1-score of 91.2% (95% CI: 88.0%–94.3%) under natural class imbalance (≈1:188), while the identity-matching module correctly identified both individuals in 458 of 487 pair-evaluable events (94.0%), with an overall pair-attribution yield of 91.8% across 499 unique confirmed events after cross-track duplicate removal. The system automatically generates structured mating logs that provide behavioral indicators for early warning and reproductive management.

title: Forecasting farmland dew intensity using deep learning models optimized via an improved snow goose algorithm
abstract: Farmland dew occurs frequently and in significant amounts. While dew plays a crucial role in enhancing fertilizer and pesticide utilization while reducing their runoff, excessive dew can hinder flowering and pollination. Prolonged dew retention on leaves also increases the risk of fungal infections in rice plants, such as rice blast disease, which can lead to subsequent yield losses. The timely forecasting of farmland dew intensity for the following day can effectively mitigate the related adverse impacts on agricultural production. This study provides critical insights for preliminary decisions on crop foliar humidity, as well as the optimal concentration and application timing of foliar fertilizers and pesticides. Multiyear (2011–2021) continuous observational data on farmland dew and meteorological factors are used to develop a hybrid deep learning model (improved snow goose algorithm (ISGA)–variational mode decomposition (VMD) –convolutional neural network (CNN) –bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) –support vector machine (SVM)) for forecasting the dew intensity 12 h in advance (the following morning). The predictive performance of the ISGA-VMD-CNN-BiLSTM-SVM model was compared with that of linear and physical models. The results demonstrate that the deep learning model achieved an R2 of 0.9266, significantly outperforming the linear model (0.3926) and physical model (0.3061). The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) between the predicted and observed dew intensities was only 7.15%, with the forecast accuracy reaching 95.58%. The proposed hybrid deep learning model yields advanced forecast-style predictions of dew intensity. Compared with conventional linear models, physical models and existing machine learning methods, this model uses fewer types of meteorological input parameters and achieves obviously higher prediction accuracy. This model provides a novel methodological framework for dew forecasting in agricultural management.

title: Multi-site benchmarking of deep reinforcement learning for forecast-informed irrigation decision-making in paddy rice
abstract: Forecast-informed paddy irrigation must balance water saving, drainage reduction, and yield protection, but comparative evidence across climates is limited. We benchmarked Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Dueling Deep Q-Network (D3QN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Rewarded-Region Replay (R3) in one paddy simulation across 15 site-crop combinations in six agroclimatic zones of China. Each policy was trained on synthetic seasons under three random seeds and evaluated on 105 observed site-years against full irrigation (FI), three deterministic forecast-driven rules, a tuned forecast threshold, and a perfect-foresight dynamic programming (DP) reference. The learned policies reduced seasonal irrigation by 12.4%–16.2% relative to FI, versus 5.4%–7.9% for the rules and 4.7% for the tuned forecast threshold, and raised rainfall utilization efficiency from 0.56 to 0.66–0.69; mean simulated potential yield loss was 0.03%–0.13%. The two value-based methods used the least water (350.3 mm for DQN and 350.8 mm for D3QN) and PPO the most (366.2 mm), while the two actor-critic methods incurred the lowest simulated yield loss (0.03% for R3 and 0.04% for PPO); neither the DQN-D3QN nor the PPO-R3 difference was significant in irrigation or simulated yield loss. Water depth and forecast rainfall jointly governed the switch from waiting to irrigating, but at a given depth the actor-critic methods required more forecast rainfall than the value-based methods to keep waiting. Under stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis of TOPSIS rankings (SMAA-TOPSIS), the leading policy changed with management priorities: DQN led at 9 of the 15 site-crop combinations where irrigation or drainage volume carried the most weight, and PPO and R3 together led at 9 where simulated yield loss did. Perfect-foresight DP reduced irrigation by 30.5% relative to FI, and the learned policies captured 47.8% of that saving, leaving a mean 66.6 mm gap to DP. The benchmark provides a reference protocol for comparing forecast-informed irrigation policies across climates.

title: MPRT-DETR: multi-platform real-time rice panicle detection and counting based on the transformer method and complex field imagery
abstract: Automatic and accurate detection and counting of rice panicles provide an important phenotypic basis for high-throughput rice monitoring and yield-related trait assessment. However, the accuracy and robustness of existing methods are often compromised by the challenges inherent to complex field conditions. These challenges include scale variations across multi-platform imagery (proximal vs. UAV), morphological diversity across cultivars and growth stages, and environmental effects such as uneven illumination and dense canopy occlusion. To overcome these hurdles, we constructed a comprehensive, multi-platform RGB image dataset that captures the period from heading to maturity for multiple cultivars, and encompasses a broad range of phenotypic variations and environmental conditions representative of real-world agricultural settings. In addition, we propose the Multi-Platform Real-Time Rice Panicle Detection and Counting Transformer (MPRT-DETR) for rice panicle detection and counting under complex field conditions. The proposed MPRT-DETR is developed as a task-oriented adaptation of RT-DETR for complex field rice panicle detection and incorporates four coordinated modifications: (1) an FEM that extends an illumination-adaptive enhancement framework by integrating WTConv and training-time label enhancement; (2) a FasterNet-based feature extraction network augmented with EMA; (3) an LBFM that reorganizes multi-scale aggregation through bidirectional feature fusion and lightweight DySample and ADown operators; and (4) a lightweight QEH designed in this study for quantity-aware adaptive query-capacity allocation. Comprehensive evaluations show that, compared with the baseline RT-DETR, MPRT-DETR reduces the parameter count by 22.30 % and GFLOPs by 32.50 %, while mAP50 and mAP50–95 increase by 11.52 and 16.43 percentage points, respectively. For panicle counting, the model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9453, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 16.2, and a relative Root Mean Square Error (rRMSE) of 14.43 % on the primary test set. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MPRT-DETR for rice panicle detection and counting under diverse field imaging conditions. Overall, MPRT-DETR provides an efficient approach for image-based rice panicle phenotyping and may serve as an upstream component for future plot-level yield-related trait assessment and breeding applications. Our code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/Agricultural-DL/MPRT-DETR.

title: Enhancing pesticide-likeness prediction via multimodal deep learning ensemble framework
abstract: Pesticide-likeness prediction is a critical task in agrochemical research and design. However, existing methods are often constrained by negative sample selection bias and overreliance on supervised learning. To address these challenges, we propose RGG, a multimodal deep learning ensemble framework that integrates Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Graph Convolutional Attention Network (GCAN) to synergistically capture molecular sequence patterns, topological features, and multimodal correlations. The positive samples were collected from the British Crop Production Council (BCPC) database, whereas the negative samples were selected from the ZINC20 database through Hao’s Rule prescreening and Butina clustering. The framework leverages a voting mechanism to harmonize the predictive strengths of heterogeneous models, thereby balancing classification robustness and generalization capability. Experimental results demonstrate that the RGG model outperformed all individual submodels on the validation sets of the 10-fold cross-validation. This improvement is reflected in a 5.33 % increase in average accuracy, along with gains of 5.05 % in precision and 5.46 % in recall. In independent testing, RGG exhibited potential for prioritizing novel bioactive molecules (AUC = 0.81). RGG generates continuous pesticide-likeness scores for candidate ranking, with a less polarized score distribution than the supervised submodels on the sampled molecules. Additional sensitivity analyses showed that the supervised model was robust to moderate changes in the clustering cutoff and benefited from diversity-oriented negative-sample selection. Furthermore, the framework supports multi-label functional categorization (fungicides, insecticides, herbicides) and enables interpretable predictions through attention mechanisms, highlighting molecular fragments associated with the model predictions. This work proposes a precision-oriented and interpretable methodology for pesticide-likeness prediction, advancing the application of deep learning in agrochemical molecular design. We also developed a web application to facilitate the use of our model: https://rgg.pianlab.team/jobs.

title: GNN-Bézier-RP: A joint path-planning method integrating graph neural networks and Bézier-curve obstacle avoidance for safflower picking with a parallel manipulator
abstract: To address irregular target distributions, local obstacle interference, and insufficient trajectory smoothness in safflower picking path planning, this study proposes a global–local integrated path-planning method for a Delta parallel manipulator. The method couples Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based global picking-order planning with Bézier-curve-based local obstacle-avoidance correction. During global planning, an improved GNN encoder models target–obstacle spatial relationships among mature safflower capitula, obstacle points, and the non-entry region, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) decoder generates the picking visiting sequence. During local correction, cubic Bézier control-point optimization modifies trajectory segments with potential obstacle conflicts, and minimum-jerk smoothing improves motion continuity. Simulation results show that, under the Active Search strategy, the proposed GNN-LSTM model obtained normalized path lengths of 7.507, 11.711, and 15.857 for the 20-, 30-, and 40-point settings, respectively. After local obstacle-avoidance correction, the path-growth cost remained within 0.037–0.078. Laboratory validation further showed that the actual path lengths changed from 751.6 cm, 1178.6 cm, and 1585.9 cm to 784.23 cm, 1202.95 cm, and 1693.0 cm, respectively, while the total execution times decreased from 38.40 s, 54.36 s, and 74.16 s to 30.24 s, 47.52 s, and 58.60 s. The planned trajectory execution success rates were 91.67%, 88.89%, and 87.50%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the coupled GNN–Bézier strategy is effective for safflower picking under the tested simulation and laboratory conditions, improving local obstacle-avoidance feasibility, motion continuity, and trajectory execution efficiency.

title: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning for dual-arm robotic pear blossom pollination in dense orchard environments
abstract: Pear blossoms are densely distributed and flower within a relatively short period, imposing stringent efficiency requirements on robotic pollination systems to complete multiple targets within a limited operational window. In unstructured pear orchards, irregular blossom distributions and overlapping reachable workspaces of the two manipulators tightly couple target allocation, workload coordination, shared-workspace conflict avoidance, and continuous motion control, making dual-arm pollination inherently a hierarchical decision-making problem. To address these coupled challenges, this study proposes a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework for dual-arm robotic pollination in dense pear blossom environments. At the high level, a Transformer-JointQ scheduler models the interactions between candidate pear blossom targets and dual-arm states and evaluates feasible target combinations through joint state–action values, thereby enabling coordinated target selection for both manipulators under dense-target conditions. At the low level, PCCS-MATD3 dynamically adjusts control preferences while incorporating temporal smoothness and dual-arm coordination constraints into policy optimization, improving motion stability and coordination during continuous execution. Simulation experiments show that Transformer-JointQ achieves task completion rates of 99.5%, 98.5%, and 99.0% for scenarios containing 6, 10, and 15 target pear blossoms, respectively, while maintaining high workload balance; meanwhile, PCCS-MATD3 achieves a 99% task completion rate in low-level evaluations and improves motion smoothness and dual-arm coordination without compromising execution efficiency. Field experiments in a real pear orchard further validate the feasibility of the proposed framework under natural illumination, irregular blossom distributions, occlusions, and environmental disturbances. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective hierarchical decision-making approach for coordinated autonomous dual-arm pollination in dense pear blossom environments.

title: Forecasting future individual-tree growth using explainable machine learning across northern Chinese larch forests
abstract: Accurately forecasting tree growth under climate change is essential for adaptive forest management, yet the ability of machine-learning models to predict future growth beyond the calibration period remains poorly evaluated. Using 615 trees and 1,230 increment cores collected from six Larix gmelinii var. principis-rupprechtii forests across northern China, we reconstructed annual basal area increment (BAI) series and developed a tree-level dataset spanning 2000–2023. Tree age, previous-year diameter at breast height (DBH), competition index (CI), and multi-temporal climatic variables were integrated into Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models and compared with a linear mixed-effects model (LMM). Both machine-learning models substantially outperformed the LMM, achieving cross-validation R2 values of 0.45–0.74 and successfully reproducing interannual growth variability. Temporal extrapolation reduced predictive performance relative to conventional cross-validation, but both models retained robust forecasting skill under unseen future conditions. Variable-importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses revealed that previous-year DBH, tree age, and competition intensity were the most influential predictors of BAI, whereas climatic effects were region-specific, nonlinear, and frequently lagged. Future projections under Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585 scenarios indicated generally stable growth during 2024–2028, with differences among sites exceeding differences among climate scenarios. Our results demonstrate that explainable machine learning can provide robust near-term forecasts of individual-tree growth beyond the calibration period and highlight temporal extrapolation as a critical component of ecological forecasting.
